pages.title: Exceptional Family Member Program
pages.text:
# Exceptional Family Member Program

We support military families with special medical and/or educational needs and ensure availability of care during transitions to improve families' quality of life.

## How To Get Started
The Exceptional Family Member Program is comprised of 3 components:

## Eligibility Identification & Enrollment
#### Eligible Exceptional Family Members Include:

- Dependent(s) of an active duty service member
- Spouse, child, or parent
- Resides with the sponsor (51%)
- Requires medical specialty care _or_
- Chronic medical condition requiring more than annual visits with a primary care physician
- Eligible for early intervention services (IFSP)
- Eligible for special education or related services (IEP)

#### Required form needed for registration:

- DD Form 2792 (all family members)
- DD Form 2792-1 (children with an Individualized Family Services Plan or Individualized Education Program)

Supplemental documentation needed as applicable (i.e., IFSP, IEP, etc.)

Completed forms can be submitted to the local EFMP office or Headquarters EFMP at hqmc.efmp@usmc.mil.

All forms can be downloaded from the [DoD Forms Management Program](https://www.esd.whs.mil/directives/forms/).

## Assignment Coordination
When a family member's specific medical or educational needs are documented via the DD2792 and DD2792-1, HQMC EFMP Assignment specialist use the information to match documented needs to the capability of the proposed PCS location. While the military's mission guides these assignments, when MMOA/MMEA/RAM and EFMP work together, the goal is to find an assignment that supports mission, career progression and family member needs.

Schedule an Assignment Consultation by emailing hqmc.efmp@usmc.mil

## Family Support
Exceptional Family Member Program professionals help families become their own best advocates by providing:

- Information and Referrals
- Helping families successfully transition before, during and after a PCS.
- Supporting families with non-clinical case management.
- Connecting families to important resources and services, such as the School Liaison Officer.

## PCSing?
Moving from one duty station to another can be stressful.

- Ensure your EFMP enrollment paperwork is current. HQMC EFMP Assignment Case Managers utilize the DD 2792 and DD 2792-1 on file to determine the appropriateness of the proposed assignment. Ensuring your paperwork is accurate benefits the timeliness of the screening and helps to put you in a location where family members have access to needed care.

- Share your needs and concerns with your Family Caseworker.

- Request 3-months of medication.

- Visit usmc-mccs.org for MCCS events, services, and support for you and your family.

- Follow your local MCCS Facebook and Instagram to stay connected to your military community and learn about events, resources, and programs offered.

## Command Resources
Providing military leadership with the resources and knowledge they need to help support their Marines and their families.

[Operations Analysis Directorate Report](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=460e2fa5-834f-4485-9189-a3bf2a156274&v=1): Analysis of the Impact of Exceptional Family Member Program Enrollment on Individual Marine Career Progression and Promotion

[Inspector General Checklist](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=98906af9-947d-42d9-9955-557d951fb7cb&v=1)

[EFMP Brief for Leaders](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=acd24733-03c9-4e95-822d-8d5c06f1fda2&v=1)

[EFMP Continuation on Location](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=0e811b63-edd3-4f07-aea0-0eac65f90ecf&v=1)

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find quick answers to common questions about our services here.

### Q: How does enrollment in EFMP affect military assignments or postings?

Enrollment in EFMP ensures consideration of a family member's needs during military assignments with the goal to place families in locations that can support those needs.

### Q: What specific services and support does EFMP offer family members with special needs?

EFMP offers various support services, including information, referrals, and case management. Some families may be eligible for respite care.

### Q: How does EFMP impact travel or relocation, especially concerning healthcare access?

EFMP helps facilitate necessary healthcare access during travel or relocation by making medical case management referrals to TRICARE.

### Q: Does EFMP enrollment qualify me for Priority Housing?

Some individuals enrolled in EFMP will be eligible for priority housing. This status will be listed on your official enrollment letter and is part of the initial and updated enrollment process.

### Q: How often should information be updated or reassessed within the EFMP system?

Families should update EFMP enrollment every 3 years or when there are changes in the family member's medical or educational needs.

### Q: How do I disenroll from the program?

If the family member is no longer a dependent, update DEERS and contact hqmc.efmp@usmc.mil to request disenrollment. If the family member's medical and/or education condition has resolved, update DD 2792 and DD 2792-1, if applicable and submit with a request for disenrollment. If the condition still exists, we will not be able to facilitate the disenrollment, as EFMP is a DoD mandatory enrollment program, when qualifying conditions are present.

### Q: Are there resources available to help navigate the program or advocate for specific needs?

The Exceptional Family Member Program has Family Support professionals who can assist families in navigating the program, accessing resources, and learning how to advocate for their needs.

### Q: How is personal and medical information handled within the EFMP?

Personal and medical information within the EFMP is treated with strict confidentiality and follows privacy regulations.

### Q: What can families do if they disagree with a decision made within the EFMP?

Families can address disagreements or concerns about EFMP decisions through established channels, often involving the EFMP office or higher-level appeals processes.

### Q: What is Respite Care?

Respite Care is a non-entitlement benefit intended to provide brief rest periods for the primary caregiver(s).

### Q: Am I able to schedule an appointment?

Yes. Contact the Family Support specialist at your local Exceptional Family Member Program to schedule an appointment.

Contact: Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP)
Address: 2034 Barnett Ave, Suite 104, Quantico, VA 22134
Phone: 703-784-9395
Email: QuanticoEfmpOffice@usmc.mil
Hours:
- Monday–Friday: 8:00am - 4:30pm

# Family Advocacy Program

We help service members and their families foster strong and meaningful relationships through skill-building classes and workshops.

## Classes and Workshops
Learn life skills that help strengthen your relationships.

Classes and workshops are available through the Family Advocacy Program (FAP).

Register for classes and workshops by using the "Upcoming Events" calendar located on the FAP webpage.

Not all classes and workshops are available at all installations.

**Anger Management**

This eight-week course teaches life skills that help you manage your anger and identify the stress related triggers in the workplace, relationships, and other life situations.

* Stress
* Empathy
* Response
* Self-talk
* Assertiveness
* Expectations
* Forgiveness
* Time-out

**Grow Parenting**

This class offers eight sessions that help parents develop life skills in the following areas:

* Praise and Encouragement: How to communicate with your child in appropriate ways.
* Managing Emotions: Understand how to help your child manage his or her emotions.
* Healthy Lifestyles: Developing healthy routines and schedules in your home.
* Managing Stress: How to manage stress and your reactions due to anger.
* Physical Health: How to promote an active lifestyle for you and your child.

**POWER Workshop**

Discover the dynamics of power and control techniques and their negative effect on relationships. In this 8-hour workshop you will learn to recognize how those techniques can result in destructive and sometimes abusive behaviors.

* Enhance Communication
* Manage Stress
* Resolve Conflict

**Seven Principles for Making Marriage Work**

This one-day workshop is designed for relationships of all kinds, focused on communication, repair, and deeper understanding.

* Grow Stronger
* Feel Closer
* Build Healthier Connections

**Stress Management / Warrior Maintenance**

Discover what stress is and how it influences behavior in the workplace, relationships, and life's challenges.

**Within My Reach**

This workshop explores the dynamics of healthy relationships.

* Enhance Communication
* Manage Stress
* Resolve Conflict

## Problematic Sexual Behaviors in Child and Youth
Free counseling services and support to military families.

Problematic Sexual Behaviors in Child & Youth (PSBCY) refers to behaviors initiated by children and youth under the age of 18 that involve sexual body parts (genitals, anus, buttocks, or breasts) in a manner that deviates from normative or typical sexual behavior and are developmentally inappropriate or potentially harmful to the individual initiating the behavior, the individual(s) impacted by the behavior or others.

Sexual behaviors initiated by a child or youth under the age of 18 are more likely to deviate from normative or typical sexual behavior and be developmentally inappropriate and/or potentially harmful when they are characterized by one or more of the following:

* Occur at a higher frequency than is typical given the child's or youth's age and development.
* Are preoccupying or are a greater focus of the child's or youth's interactions and interests than other behaviors.
* Interfere with the child's or youth's social development and/or general functioning.
* Do not respond to caregiver or other adult intervention.
* Involve sexual knowledge, language and/or behaviors that are inappropriate for the child's or youth's chronological or developmental age.
* Include aggression, force, threats, or coercion.
* Include intrusive sexual behavior, such as penetration.
* Are deliberative rather than spontaneous or exploratory in nature.
* Include alcohol or other mind-altering substances.
* Involve aggressive or violent pornography.
* Engender strong upset feelings in any other child or youth involved in the behaviors.
* Are non-mutual.

Problematic sexual behavior usually takes place when a child feels anxious or angry, is reacting to a traumatic experience, is overly curious after seeing sexual materials, is seeking attention, is trying to imitate others, or is merely trying to calm him or herself.

Parents, caregivers, educators, and professionals should approach problematic sexual behaviors with sensitivity and address them in a supportive and non-punitive manner.

Contact your local Family Advocacy for more information, support, and counseling.

## What is domestic abuse?
Domestic abuse is the use, attempted use, or threatened use of force or violence against an intimate partner. An intimate partner is a current or former spouse, a person with whom the abuser shares a child or common domicile, or a person who is in a romantic relationship with the abuser.

Examples of domestic abuse include, but are not limited to, taking your cell phone or keys, not allowing you to leave a location, controlling what you wear or who you speak to, limiting your access to money, name calling, pushing, hitting, sexual contact without your consent.

If you or someone you know is dealing with domestic abuse, contact the Family Advocacy office.

## Reporting Options
**Reporting Instructions**

1. **Unrestricted**
A person who has experienced domestic abuse who wants to pursue an official investigation of an incident should report to their chain of command, the Family Advocacy Program (FAP), or law enforcement.

2. **Restricted**
Restricted reporting allows an adult who has experienced or is experiencing domestic abuse to disclose the details of their abuse and receive medical care, counseling, and FAP advocacy without command or law enforcement involvement. Those electing to make a restricted report must report the abuse to a FAP clinician, FAP advocate, and in some states a DoD healthcare provider.

# Family Member Employment Assistance Program

The Family Member Employment Assistance Program (FMEAP) supports military spouses and dependent family members with career readiness tools, resources, and services.

## Not sure where to begin? Start here.
#### Eligibility, Services, and Support

The Family Member Employment Assistance Program (FMEAP) is designed to provide support and resources to family members, including spouses, of military service members to help them pursue and sustain meaningful employment despite the challenges of the military lifestyle.

## Eligibility, Services, and Support
#### **Eligibility**

The primary beneficiaries of the Family Member Assistance Program (FMEAP):

*   Military spouses of active-duty service members.
*   Dependent family member of active-duty service members.

#### **Getting Started**

Connect with your local installation's FMEAP office. This will allow you to schedule an introductory meeting and learn more about the program.

Attend FMEAP workshops.

Register for the Military Spouse Employment Partnership. Registration can provide you with access to a network of employer partners.

Explore MyCAA. If you're eligible and interested in pursuing further education, start the application process for the MyCAA scholarship.

Stay engaged.

#### **Available Services**

*   Career Advising & Coaching
*   Education, Entrepreneurial & Training Resources
*   Individual Career Assessment & Planning
*   Interviewing Skills
*   Job Search Strategies
*   Resume Assistance
*   Salary Negotiations
*   Volunteer & Skills Development
*   Career Workshops

## Upcoming Events
[Create a Master Resume Workshop](/activity/f5916037-5645-48cb-93f9-3c99b5d8b7ba) - Nov 9, 09:00am - 12:00pm

[Create a Master Resume Workshop](/activity/aa703b50-b658-4d07-9547-5c6417f84b0b) - Dec 2, 01:00pm - 04:00pm

## Resources, Programs & Information
#### SpouseWorks

Discover a trusted career and education support in one place.

**Welcome, military spouses!**

The Office of Spouse Employment introduces **SpouseWorks** (formerly SECO).

SpouseWorks brings all your trusted career and education support into one easy-to-navigate platform.

*   **Career Coaching & Advice:** Navigate every stage of your career journey.  

*   **Job Opportunities:** Find employers looking to hire military spouses.  

*   **Education & Funding:** Discover scholarships, fellowships, and training.

Connect to these valuable resources at [SpouseWorks](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/).

Learn more about [SpouseWorks](https://spouseworks.militaryonesource.mil/portal/article/welcome-to-spouseworks) through FAQs and related articles.

#### SpouseWorks Scholarship

Explore a workforce development program that provides up to $4,000 in financial assistance.

[Learn More](https://mycaa.militaryonesource.mil/mycaa/)

#### Military Spouse Employer Partnership (MSEP)

The Military Spouse Employer Partnership connects military spouses with hundreds of partner employers who have committed to recruit, hire, promote and retain military spouses.

[Learn More](https://msepjobs.militaryonesource.mil/msep/)

#### Military Spouse Licensure Reimbursement (MSLR)

If your career requires a professional license or certification, you may be eligible for up to $1,000 in reimbursement for licensure and certification costs resulting from relocations within the United States or from OCONUS to stateside.

Moving across the country – or around the world – can be a great adventure.

pages.title: Marine Corps Family Team Building
pages.text:
# Marine Corps Family Team Building

We empower Marines, families, and units with valuable resources and problem-solving skills to help them navigate the demands of military life.

## Eligibility & How To Get Started
#### Eligibility and Getting Started

Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) offers comprehensive support to the entire military community through a variety of workshops and training programs.

**Eligibility for participation in our program extends to individuals across various segments of the military community. This includes:**

- Active Duty Service Members: Including all branches of the military, all ranks.
- Department of Defense (DoD) Employees
- Spouses of Military Personnel

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

1. **Identify Individual Needs:** Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB program offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.

## Upcoming Events
Various workshops and training events are scheduled throughout the year, including Family Readiness Advisory & Assistance Training, L.I.N.K.S.

## Programs, Resources & Support
#### Unit, Personal and Family Readiness Program (UPFRP)

Marine Corps Family Team Building provides training in support of the Unit, Personal, & Family Readiness Program (UPFRP).

Training includes Family Readiness Command Team Training (FRCTT), Deployment Readiness and Uniformed Readiness Coordinator (DRC/URC) training, and Family Readiness Command Team Advisor/Assistant (FRCTA/FRA) training.

The UPFRP Family Readiness Program Training (FRPT) provides training to UPFRP personnel to include:

- Family Readiness Command Team Training (FRCTT)
- Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC)
- Uniformed Readiness Coordinator (URC)
- Family Readiness Command Team Advisors (FRCTA)
- Family Readiness Assistant (FRA)

The UPFRP provides comprehensive support and resources to Marines and families, with the goal to equip service members and their families with the skills necessary to overcome challenges and thrive during their military life journey.

For information about volunteering with your unit's UPFRP, please contact your DRC or URC.

#### LifeSkills Training

LifeSkills Training classes are designed to equip Service Members and their families with the necessary skills for successful interactions, both at work and home, ultimately leading to positive outcomes in all areas of life.

Workshops are comprehensive collection of personal and professional skill-building classes, promoting successful outcomes in various life challenges.

- **Four Lenses:** This interactive workshop focuses on four temperament styles that greatly influence one's life.

- **Five Love Languages:** This workshop is based on the #1 New York Times bestseller written by Dr. Millions of couples have learned the simple way to express their feelings and bring joy back into marriage.

- **Real Relationships:** This workshop helps to identify the hallmarks of meaningful relationships and how to build skills to make them stronger.

- **Say What?:** This workshop is design to teach valuable communication strategies to help individuals communicate more effectively fostering healthier relationships.

- **Basic Anger Management:** Although disagreements and anger are a normal part of life, violent expressions of feelings detract from personal and professional relationships and can negatively affect the efficient functioning and morale of Marine Corps units, individuals, families, and communities.

- **Basic Stress Management:** Learn what stress is and how to manage it by changing your response to it. Learn to apply helpful techniques to ease the weight of stress within your life. Learn how to apply a problem solving method to take action in high-stress situations.

- **Living My Best Life: Bridging the Generation Gap:** Bridging the Generation Gap shows participants the unique characteristics of the many generations that exist today providing a foundation to enable improved communication across generations through increased knowledge of generational characteristics, influences, and priorities.

- **Living My Best Life: Attitudes & Actions:** This course is designed to encourage military members and their families to maintain a positive focus and be engaged in their homes, at work, and in their communities.

- **Ready, Set, Prepare:** This workshop contains information regarding actions that service members and families should take to be informed and prepared in the event of natural and man-made hazards.

- **Prevention & Relationship Enhancement Program (PREP):** PREP 8.0 is designed to help couples achieve their relationship goals.

Not all workshops are available at all locations.

Please contact your MCFTB office for workshop schedule and availability.

#### Readiness and Deployment Support

Readiness and Deployment Support provides service members and their families with the knowledge and skills to prepare and successfully navigate all phases of deployments.

The Readiness & Deployment Support workshops are designed to equip Service Members and their families with essential life skills necessary to effectively overcome the anticipated and often un-foreseen challenges that suddenly arise during deployments.

**Workshops:**

- **Pre-Deployment Brief for Marines & Families:** This brief is held per unit request 30 to 45 days prior to a service members deployment. For Individual Augments (IA) or short notice deployments, please call MCFTB for a personalized appointment.

- **Family Care Plan:** Learn who needs a family care plan, what should be included in an effective family care plan and how to construct one.

- **Mid-Deployment Success:** This workshop is designed to promote deployment success for the spouse or significant other at home and includes suggestions for fun things to do, goal setting, and resources. The workshop is an excellent opportunity to assess progress thus far, get new ideas for continued success, and network with other Marine Corps spouses and significant others.

- **Mid-Deployment Kids:** This workshop is designed to promote deployment success for kids, including reactions to deployment, ways parents can help their kids feel connected to the deployed parent, and resources to help you and your child thrive during a deployment.

- **Return and Reunion for Parents & Extended Families:** Spouses and significant others of returning Marines are eager to discuss homecoming anticipation, expectations, and concerns. This is a brief that is required to be provided to remain-behind family members and is part of the required Pre-Deployment Agreement form.

- **Return and Reunion for Parents & Kids:** Held in conjunction with Return and Reunion Workshops for spouses, MCFTB work with children ages 5 and up to help them prepare for their service member's homecoming in a fun and interactive setting.

- **Reintegration Success:** This educational workshop provides a forum for couples to assess their recent deployment experience, address the effect of reintegration on a relationship, and assess the level of relationship satisfaction.

Not all workshops are available at all locations.

Contact your MCFTB office for schedule and availability.

#### Lifestyle Insights, Networking, Knowledge, and Skills (L.I.N.K.S.)

This is a volunteer-based, team-mentoring program, designed to teach participants about navigating the unique challenges of life in the military.

# Personal Financial Management

We provide you and your family with professional training and guidance to help you manage money successfully.

## Get Started with Your Personal Finances
Taking the first steps toward financial stability and your future.

**Eligibility and First Steps**

Eligibility for participation in our program extends to individuals across various sections of the military community.

- Service Members
- Family Members
- DoD Employees

Getting started is easy!

**Contact us.**
Get professional guidance and support tailored to your financial goals.

**Make an appointment.**
Schedule your personalized financial consultation today! Making an appointment is easy – just reach out to our program office and take the first step towards financial success.

**Register for workshops or courses.**
Sign up for our workshops and classes to enhance your financial literacy! Register now to secure your spot and gain valuable insights into managing your money effectively.

**Explore our webpage.**
Discover helpful financial tools and resources provided by the Personal Financial Management Program. From workshop schedules to helpful resources, everything you need to get started is just a click away!

## Financial Services
Unlock your financial potential with our comprehensive services!

Contact us today to learn more about the services offered and how we can help you achieve your financial goals.

- Blended Retirement System
- Car Buying
- Consumer Awareness
- Continuation Pay
- Couple Financial Counseling
- Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
- Credit / Debt Management
- Developing a Spending Plan
- Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
- Individual Financial Counseling
- Major Purchases
- Military Pay & Benefits
- Retirement Planning
- Survivor Benefits Plan
- Thrift Savings Plan
- Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

## Become a Command Financial Specialist
Command Financial Specialists (CFS) are a vital resource for Marines, offering support throughout their careers.

In accordance with MCO 1700.37, the minimum requirements for assignment as a unit Command Financial Specialist are:

- Must be an E6, WO, O-1, and above.
- Have at least one year remaining at your present duty station.
- Highly motivated.
- Financially stable.
- Have no record of Letters of Indebtedness/Non-Sufficient Funds/NJP/Poor performance counseling above the rank of LCPL.
- Successfully complete the Leading Marines Course and MCI's 3420 and 3422 on Personal Financial Management.
- Participate in continuing education such as CFS forums and refresher training.

You do not need a degree in financial planning to succeed as a CFS.

The most successful CFSs are those who enjoy the process of identifying financial needs and thrive on the challenge of finding solutions.

As a Command Financial Specialist, you will help Marines and their families learn about managing money and making smart financial choices.

For more information contact your MCCS Personal Financial Manager.

## Financial Resources
Tools and services that support your financial well-being.

**Budgeting Tools**

Contact your local Personal Financial Management Program office for helpful tools for managing your money to take charge of your finances.

- [Financial Well-Being Assessment](https://finred.usalearning.gov/FWBA)
- [Spending Plan Worksheet](https://finred.usalearning.gov/assets/downloads/FINRED-Spendingplan-TK.pdf)
- [Personal Net Worth Tracker](https://finred.usalearning.gov/ToolsAndAddRes/NetWorth)
- [Financial Calculators](https://finred.usalearning.gov/ToolsAndAddRes/Calculators)
- [Sen$e App](https://finred.usalearning.gov/ToolsAndAddRes/Sen$e)

**Financially Fit Kids**

Providing kids with financial skills help them avoid debt and prepare for big expenses and the future.

Learn more about tips and tools available to help raise [Financially Fit Kids](https://www.milspousemoneymission.org/military-spouse-raising-financial-fit-kids/).

- Values & Habits
- Self Assessment
- Communication Skills
- Goal Setting
- All About Allowances
- System for Saving
- Create a Spending Plan
- Tips & Videos

**Thrift Savings Plan**

Designed to help your build financial security for the future with one of the finest retirement plans.

[Thrift Savings Plan](https://www.tsp.gov/)

**Blended Retirement System**

The Blended Retirement System (BRS) is a way for service members to save for retirement, introduced in 2018. Unlike the retirement services in the past where only those who served for 20 years received a pension, the BRS offers benefits for almost all service members.

The BRS combines a regular pension for those who serve at least 20 years with a savings plan similar to a civilian 401(k), where the government also adds money to your savings.

The BRS makes it possible for military personnel to start building their retirement savings early in their careers, whether they plan to stay for the full length of service or not.

Learn more about the Blended Retirement System at [Blended Retirement System](https://militarypay.defense.gov/BlendedRetirement/)

**Continuation Pay**

Continuation Pay under the Blended Retirement System (BRS) is a one-time bonus offered to military members who agree to extend their service beyond their current enlistment period.

This bonus serves as an incentive for service members to continue their military career at mid-career points.

Accepting continuation pay comes with a commitment to serve for an additional number of years, and failing to fulfill this commitment may require the service member to repay the received bonus.

[Continuation Pay](https://finred.usalearning.gov/assets/downloads/FINRED-ContinuationPay-FS.pdf)

**Managing Stress**

- Relationship Concerns
- Work Stressors
- Life Stressors
- Trauma
- EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
- Grief and Loss
- Sadness
- Worry
- Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
- Adjustment
- Crisis Intervention
- Sleep Hygiene
- Parent-Child Communication

Community Counseling

**Budgeting for Education**

Whether you're looking to earn a college degree, obtain a certification, or improve your skills, there are resources designed to support your personal and professional growth, preparing you for success both in the Marine Corps and in civilian life.

Contact the Education Center and speak with a coordinator.

**Family Member Employment Assistance**

Connect with your local Family Member Employment Assistance office to schedule an introductory meeting and learn more about the program.

**Available Services:**

- Career Advising & Coaching
- Career Workshops
- Education, Entrepreneurial & Training Resources
- Individual Career Assessment & Planning
- Interviewing Skills
- Job Search Strategies
- Resume Assistance
- Salary Negotiations
- Volunteer & Skills Development

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**Is there a fee associated with participating in the PFMP offered by MCCS?**

The services provided by PFMP are offered free of charge to eligible individuals and their families.

**How do I schedule an appointment for financial counseling through the PFMP?**

To schedule a counseling session, individuals can contact their local PFMP office or visit the office for appointment scheduling options.

**Are the PFMP workshops and seminars available online for remote participation?**

Yes, PFMP offers online workshops and seminars to accommodate service members and DoD employees stationed in various locations.

**Can family members participate in PFMP workshops and counseling sessions?**

Yes. Family members can participate in PFMP workshops and counseling sessions. Register for a workshop by using the calendar or contact the Personal Financial Management to register and schedule a counseling session.

**Is financial counseling provided by certified professionals?**

Yes, PFMP financial counselors are trained and certified to provide financial education, counseling, and assistance to service members and their families.

**Can DoD employees who are not military service members also access PFMP services through MCCS?**

Yes, PFMP services are available to DoD civilian employees to help them manage their personal finances effectively.

Address: 3019 Embry Loop, Quantico, VA 22134
Email: mccsquanticoppdregistration@usmc.mil

# Community Counseling

We provide non-medical counseling services and help service members and their families develop skills to manage life's stressors and challenges.​

## Eligibility & How To Get Started
#### Getting Started

Offering support to service members and their families within the military community.

#### Getting Started

Eligibility for participation in our Community Counseling Program extends to individuals across various segments of the military community.

*   Active-Duty Service Members - All Branches
*   Civilian Expeditionary Forces
*   Spouses
*   Families
*   Children
*   Recruits

**How to get started with Community Counseling:**

1.  **Schedule an Appointment:** Contact the Community Counseling Program office and speak to a professional about scheduling an appointment with a mental health clinician.
2.  **Assessment:** A Community Counseling Program clinician will conduct an intake assessment which typically involves a structured evaluation designed to identify an individual's needs, concerns, and goals regarding their mental health and well-being.

4.  **Case Management Services:** If individuals or families are working with multiple providers and managing multiple systems, our staff and clinicians are available to assist you.

pages.text:
# Domestic Abuse

## Domestic Abuse Prevention Resources
**HOW CAN WE HELP YOU?**

[800-799-7233](tel:800-799-7233)

## What is Domestic Abuse?
Domestic abuse is the use, attempted use, or threatened use of force or violence against an intimate partner. An intimate partner is a current or former spouse, a person with whom the abuser shares a child or common domicile, or a person who is in a romantic relationship with the abuser.

Examples of domestic abuse include, but are not limited to, taking your cell phone or keys, not allowing you to leave a location, controlling what you wear or who you speak to, limiting your access to money, name calling, pushing, hitting, or sexual contact without your consent.

**Additional Links**

* [Starting Tough Conversations: Relationship Red Flags](/news/starting-tough-conversations-relationship-red-flags/)
* [Domestic Abuse Military Reporting Options • Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/family-relationships/family-life/preventing-abuse-neglect/domestic-abuse-military-reporting-options/)
* [Family Advocacy - Marine Corps Community](/marine-family-support/military-family-life/family-advocacy-program)

## I Have Experienced Domestic Abuse
It's important to know where you can go for safe, judgment-free help when you are feeling unsafe in your relationship.

Everyone who experiences domestic abuse has a unique set of circumstances and concerns. Through [your installation's](https://installations.militaryonesource.mil/?looking-for-a=program/program-service=32/focus=program) FAP, you can meet with a FAP advocate with a deep understanding about the challenges of seeking help for domestic abuse.

If you have experienced intimate partner abuse contact a FAP Advocate or FAP Clinician to learn about resources available to you and reporting options. You may be eligible to obtain a restricted report.

Victims may also decide to seek help outside the military. FAP can connect you to civilian or community-based resources, or you can visit the [National Domestic Violence Hotline](https://www.thehotline.org/) website.

**If you are experiencing domestic abuse,** visit [HERE](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/leaders-service-providers/child-abuse-and-domestic-abuse/victim-advocate-locator/) to locate the closest FAP office, or go to the [National Domestic Violence Hotline](http://www.thehotline.org/) website or call 800-799-7233. Call 911 if you are in immediate danger. If you are on a military installation, call your military law enforcement office.

Three groups of professionals may keep information about domestic abuse confidential under the restricted reporting option:

* [FAP Advocates](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/family-relationships/family-life/preventing-abuse-neglect/the-family-advocacy-program/)
* FAP clinicians
* DoD Health care providers*

Making a restricted report means:

* FAP will not notify military law enforcement.
* Command is not involved.
* You have access to the full range of FAP services, including counseling and advocacy.

You are also entitled to the protections of privileged communication with a chaplain.

To prioritize victim safet, the restricted reporting option is not availalbe if there is an immediate risk of serious harm. And the restricted reporting option does not apply to child abuse cases, which are required by law to be reported to law enforcement and child welfare services.

\* Some state-specific laws may require medical providers to report known or suspected incidents of domestic abuse to law enforcement regardless of a victim's preferences.

When an unrestricted report is made, FAP will notify both military law enforcement and the service member's military command.
Making an unrestricted report means:

* Military law enforcement will conduct an investigation of the incident, which includes contacting the alleged abuser.
* Command will be notified.
* You can seek a Military and/or Civilian Protective Order.
* You have access to the full range of FAP services, including counseling and advocacy.
* You have access to legal services on military installations.
* If a service member is separated for domestic abuse, the victim may be eligible for transitional compensation

**Additional Links**

* [Family Advocacy Program: The Relationship Resource You Haven't Heard Of](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/resources/tools/domestic-abuse-victim-advocate-locator/)
* [Domestic Abuse Military Reporting Options • Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/family-relationships/family-life/preventing-abuse-neglect/domestic-abuse-military-reporting-options/)
* [Transitional Compensation: Help for Victims of Abuse • Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/family-relationships/relationships/relationship-challenges-and-divorce/transitional-compensation-help-for-victims-of-abuse/)
* [Family Advocacy Program Relationship Support • Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/programs/family-advocacy-program/)

## I Need to Talk with Someone now
FAP advocates provide crisis intervention, immediate and ongoing advocacy services, and safety planning to victims of domestic abuse and non-abusing parents of child abuse victims. To speak with someone regarding services please call your local installation's 24 hours a day, 7 days a week helpline.

**24/7 Helpline For Your Local Installation**

**Additional Links**

* [What to Expect When You Contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline • thehotline.org](https://www.thehotline.org/what-to-expect-when-you-contact-us/)

## I Want to Help Someone Else
**5 Ways to Help a Friend Who is Experiencing Domestic Abuse**

Everyone's situation is different — domestic abuse can happen to anyone and it's not their fault.

1. **Ask to connect**
   "How do you prefer we connect?"

Having a safe way to communicate is important.

2. **Stay in touch**
   "Let's play a game online."

Finding creative reasons to call, text, video chat or use social media check-ins may provide a lifeline for those who feel unsafe at home. Learn about privacy and safety tips for technology from the National Network to End Domestic Violence at [www.techsafety.org](https://www.techsafety.org/resources).

3. **Support and believe**
   "I care about you and I'm here for you, no matter what."

Remind your friend that they are not alone and that you are there for them.

4. **Chat about options**
   "Let's create a safety plan."

Options are empowering. Talk to your friend about their options for seeking help or [reporting](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/family-relationships/family-life/preventing-abuseneglect/domestic-abuse-military-reporting-options) domestic abuse in the military: Let them know that FAP [advocates](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/leaders-service-providers/child-abuse-and-domestic-abuse/victim-advocate-locator) are available 24/7 to help them think through dangerous situations and create a safety plan.

5. **Share the hotline**
   "Here is the information for that restaurant I told you about."

It may be safer for your friend if you research support options for them - such as the National Domestic Violence Hotline at [https://www.thehotline.org](https://www.thehotline.org/) - on your device, provided you feel safe doing so.

Create a secret code word, phrase or symbol that lets you know your friend is signaling for help, whether that means a call from you or for you to call the police. A call can sometimes disrupt abuse.

**Additional Links**

* [When it Comes to Domestic Abuse, Be an Upstander, Not a Bystander • Military OneSource](https://blog-brigade.militaryonesource.mil/2021/09/27/when-it-comes-to-domestic-abuse-be-an-upstander-not-a-bystander-2/)
* [Ways to Support a Domestic Violence Survivor • thehotline.org](https://www.thehotline.org/support-others/ways-to-support-a-domestic-violence-survivor/)

## I Don't Know Where To Start
Making the decision to seek help for domestic abuse can be difficult. Everyone deserves to be in a relationship that is free of abuse. If you are experiencing abuse, consider exploring your options with the National Hotline (1800-799-SAFE (7233)) or [www.thehotline.org](http://www.thehotline.org). Alternatively, you can contact your local installation [FAP Helpline](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/leaders-service-providers/child-abuse-and-domestic-abuse/victim-advocate-locator/) where a FAP Advocate can offer an additional layer of support relevant to military supportive options and resources.

Through a FAP Advocate, you will be encouraged to develop a plan for safety and will explore local resources that are relevant to your specific needs. You will also learn about your options for reporting the abuse based on your current safety and eligibility for services from military resources.

The FAP provides a variety of supportive services including prevention, home visitation, advocacy and clinical services.

* Clinical Program provides screenings, assessments, evidence-based counseling, clinical case management, and appropriate referrals.
* FAP Advocates provide crisis intervention, ongoing advocacy services, and safety planning.
* New Parent Support Program offers parenting education and home visiting services to expectant parents and families with children ages zero to five. It is staffed with home visitors who are licensed social workers, licensed counselors and/or licensed registered nurses.
* The Prevention and Education program provides education and prevention-focused services to individuals, families, and the community.

**Additional Links**

* [Domestic Abuse Military Reporting Options](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/family-relationships/family-life/preventing-abuse-neglect/domestic-abuse-military-reporting-options/)
* [Community Counseling - Marine Corps Community](https://usmc-mccs.org/services/support/community-counseling/)
* [DOD Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate Locator • Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/leaders-service-providers/child-abuse-and-domestic-abuse/victim-advocate-locator/)

## Leaders Resources
Per DODI 6400.06, Commanders have the overriding responsibility for the response to domestic abuse. They are required to respond to all known and suspected incidents of domestic abuse and support victims. DoDM 6400.01 V3 provides additional information about the IDC process. FAP provides training to Commanders and Senior Enlisted Advisors on their responsibilities per DODI 6400.06, IDC, FAP services, and local resources.

Taking care of Marines is the plan of the day, every day. Doing it well requires constant training. The Marine Corps [Warfighter Mental Readiness Playbook](/modules/media/?do=inline&id=ab2955d1-7357-42a5-839b-282b3b018703&v=4) is a guide for effective influence.

**5 Ways Command Leaders Can Unite Against Domestic Abuse**

Domestic abuse is incompatible with military values and reduces mission readiness.

As a leader, it is important that you understand your responsibility to report and respond to allegations of domestic abuse, show compassion to victims, raise awareness of domestic abuse in the military and clearly communicate the Department of Defense's commitment to ending abuse with your command.

1. **Educate yourself**

Make sure you understand your responsibility to report and respond to allegations of domestic abuse. Find more information online: [https://www.militaryonesource.mil/Leaders-End-Abuse](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/Leaders-End-Abuse)

2. **Raise awareness**

Raise awareness of domestic abuse in the military and clearly communicate the Defense Department's commitment to unite against abuse within your command. This toolkit can help: [https://www.militaryonesource.mil/abuse-help-leaders](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/abuse-help-leaders)

   Share the following resources:

   Immediate crisis support
   National Domestic Violence Hotline
   Call 800-799-7233
   [https://www.thehotline.org/](https://www.thehotline.org/)

   Local support, 24/7
Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate Locator [https://www.militaryonesource.mil/DAVALocator](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/DAVALocator)

   Support for young people between ages 13 to 26 years old
   Love is Respect | Text "LOVEIS" to 866-331-9474
   [https://www.loveisrespect.org/](https://www.loveisrespect.org/)

3. **Take action immediately**

Show anyone who reports abuse to you that you take all their concerns seriously by: • Explaining how you will address their concerns and take action • Connecting them with a FAP advocate who can help them document their abuse, make a safety plan and access military and civilian services • Offering to follow up with them (via phone call or email) to ensure they received all the services and support they need

4. **Show compassion to victims**

Tell anyone who raises a concern about abuse that you believe them, that they are not alone and that help and support are available.

5. **Unite with other leaders against abuse**

Coordinate with other command leaders and departments throughout your installation to provide consistent and easily accessible domestic violence awareness and prevention education, resources and support.

**Top 3 Things You Can Say to Help a Victim of Abuse**

* I take your concerns seriously. You are not alone in this.
* A FAP advocate can help you document the abuse, make a safety plan and access military or civilian services.
* I can follow up with you via phone or email to ensure you received all the services and support you need.

**Additional Links**

* [Warfighter Mental Readiness Playbook](/modules/media/?do=inline&id=ab2955d1-7357-42a5-839b-282b3b018703&v=4)

## Safety Alert

Computer use can be monitored and it is impossible to completely clear your browser history. If you are afraid your internet usage is being monitored, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 800-799-7233 or 800-787-3224 en Español.

# Military OneSource

Along with resources provided at the duty station, such as counselors, chaplains, and other advisors, [Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-help/non-medical-counseling/military-onesource/military-counseling-for-stress/#contact-us) can also support Service members and their families.

Military OneSource, [https://www.militaryonesource.mil/](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-help/non-medical-counseling/military-onesource/military-counseling-for-stress/#contact-us), is your connection to information, answers, and support when Marine Corps life happens.

Military OneSource is a free service to Marines (active duty, veteran, wounded/ill/injured), attached sailors, family, and naval personnel supporting Marine Units. The Military OneSource Line is a confidential phone and chat support service that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

## Crisis Signs
These signs require immediate attention. If you are experiencing any of these and need medical attention, call 911 now. For immediate help in dealing with a suicidal crisis, call the Military Crisis Line at 1-800-273-8255 and Press 1 or dial 988.

*   Thinking about hurting or killing yourself
*   Looking for ways to kill yourself
*   Talking about death, dying, or suicide
*   Self-destructive behavior, such as drug abuse, risky use of weapons, etc.

For more information, visit the [Military Crisis Line website](http://www.veteranscrisisline.net/get-help-now/military-crisis-line/).

The goal of the Military OneSource confidential support services is to help callers manage stress in all forms, ranging from relationship and career issues, to deployment and financial problems, and develop the necessary skills required to cope with the widely-varying challenges of life in the Corps.

A few of the types of help available:

*   Relationship counseling
*   Non-medical counseling for stress relief
*   Financial counseling
*   Document translation
*   Spouse scholarships, education and career benefits
*   Child care options
*   Permanent change of station moves

[Learn more](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-help/non-medical-counseling/military-onesource/military-counseling-for-stress/#contact-us) about what happens when you use Military OneSource support services.

Contact: Military OneSource Line
Phone: 1-800-342-9647
Phone (Crisis Line): 1-800-273-8255 (Press 1)
Phone (Crisis Line (Dial)): 988
Hours (Available):
- 24/7: Phone and chat support
Confidential support service
Free service to Marines, attached sailors, family, and naval personnel supporting Marine Units

# Virtual Support for Marines & Their Families

Marines and families face stress–in life, at work, in training, on deployments.

## Free, Convenient, and Effective
Marines and their families are eligible to receive up 12 free, non-medical confidential counseling sessions per issue.

Semper Support provides access to counseling for service members, as well as their families, who are geographically dispersed and/or those who may experience barriers to in-person counseling services.

## Confidential Support for Life's Challenges
Marine leaders and their unit's Operational Stress Control and Readiness (OSCAR) team members provide critical mentorship and support.

Semper Support provides virtual, non-medical counseling and referrals for Marines and their families to address stressful situations.

## The Right Help at the Right Time
Your safety is our priority.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find answers to commonly asked questions.

## How do I access Semper Support?
Contact Semper Support worldwide at 800-342-9647, or visit [https://www.militaryonesource.mil/benefits/marine-corps-semper-support/](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/benefits/marine-corps-semper-support/).

## Who is eligible for Semper Support?
- Active-duty Marines and their immediate family members.
- Reserve Marines (regardless of activation status) and their immediate family members who are listed in DEERS.
- Designated Department of Defense expeditionary civilians and their immediate family members.
- Marines and their immediate family members who are listed in DEERS for 365 days post-separation.
- Surviving spouses who have not remarried and surviving children who are listed in DEERS.

## How many counseling sessions are typically provided through Semper Support?
Semper Support typically provides up 12 free counseling sessions.

## Do I need an appointment to access Semper Support?
No appointment is needed to reach out for counseling.

## Is there a fee for using this service?
No, this is a free service.

## Why is Semper Support important for the Marine Corps?
Semper Support provides access to counseling for service members and their families who are geographically dispersed and/or those who may experience barriers to in-person counseling services.

Contact: Semper Support
Phone (Worldwide): 800-342-9647

pages.text:
# Sexual Assault Prevention and Response

## SAPR RESOURCES
**HOW CAN WE HELP YOU?**

[877-995-5247](tel:877-995-5247)

## What is Sexual Assault?
Sexual Assault is a crime.

After a sexual assault occurs, some people may want to question what someone did before, during, or after the sexual assault, which can lead to "victim blaming." The person who was assaulted is never to blame for what happened to them.

**What Is Consent . . .**

Consent is given with words or overt acts indicating a freely given agreement to the sexual contact by a "competent" person. You are considered "incompetent" if you are sleeping or incapacitated, due to alcohol or drug use, mental incapacity, or age.

**What Is NOT Consent . . .**

Lack of verbal or physical resistance is not consent. For the full legal definition of consent, please see Marine Corps Order 1752.5C.

There are a few important things to remember about consent. Consent is required for all sexual encounters, but it is the bare minimum, not what someone should be striving for when it comes to sex.

**What Offenses Are Sexual Assault?**

Sexual assault includes a broad category of sexual offenses, including rape, forcible sodomy (oral or anal sex), and other unwanted sexual contact that is aggravated, abusive, or wrongful (including unwanted and inappropriate sexual contact) or attempts to commit these acts.

## What Do I Do if I'm Sexually Assaulted?
If you were sexually assaulted, there are some things you may want to consider doing to keep yourself safe and healthy.

**Consider Taking These Steps**

* Go to a safe place away from the alleged offender.
Note: You cannot file a 'Restricted Report' if you disclose a sexual assault to PMO/law enforcement and/or previously elected to make an Unrestricted Report by signing a DD Form 2910 on the same sexual assault incident.
* Preserve evidence of the assault. For instance:
  * Do not take a shower or a bath.
  * Do not wash your hands or brush your teeth.
  * Do not clean up or remove anything from the crime scene.
* Contact a Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC), or SAPR Victim Advocate (VA), who will:
  * Keep your report confidential.
  * Inform you of the Restricted & Unrestricted reporting options.
  * Provide you with resources and support.
* Seek medical care to take care of physical injuries, risk of pregnancy, or sexually-transmitted infections.
* Request a Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) to collect evident from the assault.
* Consider a blood test or urinalysis if you suspect you were drugged. (Note: For unrestricted reports only)

**No matter where you are in the world, free and confidential help is available.**

Contact the DoD Safe Helpline - 24/7 Confidential Toll-free call at [1-877-995-5247](tel:1-877-995-5247) or at [www.safehelpline.org](http://www.safehelpline.org) and search by unit or installation name or zip code to find SAPR resources or rape crisis centers near you.

For those on or close to a USMC Installation, call your local 24/7 SAPR helpline.

## How 24/7 Support Lines Make A Difference
Survivors of military sexual assault are never alone – no matter when or where assistance is needed. Marines and their families have immediate access to resources and referrals by calling their installation's 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line.

The Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) Victim Advocates (VAs) and Sexual Assault Response Coordinators (SARCs) who staff these support lines are dedicated to getting it right. A single phone call may be the only chance SAPR VAs or SARCs get to make a difference in the life of a survivor, so they are trained to give their best effort every time.

[DOD Safe Helpline Live Chat](https://safehelpline.org/)

**24/7 Helpline For Your Local Installation**

Quantico: [703-432-9999](tel:703-432-9999)

**10 Things to Know about 24/7 Support**

1. **Anywhere** – Each United States Marine Corps (USMC) installation has a 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line to assist sexual assault survivors with appropriate care and critical information.
2. **Anytime** – 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines ring directly to cell phones held by the installation's SAPR VA or SARC.
3. **Knowledgeable** – All SAPR VAs and SARCs who answer the 24/7 Support Lines are credentialed by the Department of Defense (DOD) Sexual Assault Advocate Certification Program (D-SAACP).
4. **Dependable** – No call by a survivor ever goes unanswered. After five rings, a call to the 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line is automatically forwarded to the DOD Safe Helpline.
5. **Local** – After receiving a forwarded call, DOD Safe Helpline personnel will always try to connect the survivor back to the appropriate installation 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Line.
6. **Supportive** – Whether assisted by DOD or the installation's SAPR VA or SARC, the survivor will always be provided with immediate crisis support and referrals to appropriate services.
7. **Personal** – If requested, a credentialed SAPR VA or SARC will meet with the survivor within two hours of the initial call for any reason related to the sexual assault.
8. **Confidential** – Calls to the 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines and the DOD Safe Helpline are strictly confidential.
9. **Professional** – 24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines are audited monthly to make sure the response system is timely, efficient, and effective and to correct any identified issues.
10. **Quality Care** – The Marine Corps SAPR Program is committed to providing survivors of sexual assault with comprehensive, quality care.

24/7 Sexual Assault Support Lines have connected hundreds of survivors with a trusted, confidential source of support since 2010. Whether looking for specific information or just someone to talk to about a sexual assault, round-the-clock help is just a phone call away.

If you are deployed or stationed at a non-USMC installation, contact your SAPR VA for assistance or call the DOD Safe Helpline at [1-877-995-5247](tel:1-877-995-5247).

## Supporting a Friend after Sexual Assault
You may have a friend, loved one, or family member who was sexually assaulted.

**DO listen.**

Sometimes the best thing you can do is just be a good listener.

**DO be patient.**

Recovery from trauma does not have a set timetable.

**DON'T judge.**

People who were sexually assaulted can be scrutinized or even blamed for what happened to them. The alleged offender is 100 percent responsible for the crime.

**DON'T ask for details.**

You don't need to know the "who, what, when, where, how and why" of the assault.

**DO use phrases such as:**

"You're safe now" (only if that is true)

"I'm glad you're talking to me."

"I'm sorry it happened."

"It wasn't your fault."

"It's ok that you're reacting this way.

"It must have been really upsetting to experience that.

"I can't imagine how you must feel.'

**DON'T use phrases such as**:

"What were you wearing?"

"How much did you have to drink?"

"You're lucky that . . ."

"It'll take some time, but you'll get over it."

"I can imagine how you feel."

"Don't worry; it's going to be all right."

"Try to be strong for your children, spouse, etc."

"Calm down and try to relax."

**DO ask if they are open to getting help.**

Ask if your friend is open to seeking medical care or talking to a Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC) or Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) Victim Advocate (VA).

If your friend has just been through the assault, you may ask your friend about going to the SANE Emergency Department or offer to take your friend there yourself.

**DON'T leave them alone**.

People who are sexually assaulted are often overwhelmed with feelings, including fear, shock, helplessness, hopelessness, despair, anger, anxiety, panic, and even suicidal thoughts. Before you leave your friend, ask if you can call someone else to provide support, like a SARC or SAPR VA.

**DO take care of yourself.**

When we have a friend in need or in pain, it can be difficult not knowing how to help. [RAINN](https://www.rainn.org/articles/self-care-friends-and-family) (Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network), and the [SAFE Helpline](https://www.safehelpline.org/) have great self-care resources that can help you feel less overwhelmed.

For more information about how to help someone, visit the Sexual Assault Prevention and Response page or visit [SAFE Helpline](https://www.safehelpline.org/) for more confidential services.

## I don't know where to start
When a victim of sexual assault decides to report, it's important to understand the options available.

**Who does the SAPR Program cover?**

The SAPR Program will continue to provide services to all adult sexual assault victims who are non-intimate partners and to adults of sexual assault who are unmarried intimate partners when they are not: a current or former spouse, share a child in common, currently or previously shared a domicile, and when domestic abuse is present. If the victim falls under one the categories (spouse/child/domicile/domestic abuse) the victim will be referred to Family Advocacy Program (FAP).

**Knowing Your Options**

Service members and military dependents (18 years and older) have two options when it comes to reporting sexual assault: Unrestricted or Restricted Reporting. The person will need to fill out a [DD Form 2910](https://www.esd.whs.mil/Directives/forms/dd2500_2999/) with assistance from a Sexual Assault Prevention & Response (SAPR) Victim Advocate (VA), or Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC).

**Unrestricted Reporting** - is recommended for someone who desires a law enforcement investigation, and the support of the chain of command; unrestricted reporting provides the person with access to ALL supportive service options:

* Advocacy Services (support, information, referral, and accompaniment)
* Medical/Counseling Services
* Victims Legal Counsel
* Military Protective Order
* Civilian Protective Order
* Expedited Transfer
* CATCH Program when the name of suspect is not known by law enforcement

For an **Unrestricted Report** - Someone can disclose a sexual assault to the following people:

* SAPR Victim Advocate
* Sexual Assault Response Coordinator
* Healthcare Personnel
* Chaplain
* Victims Legal Counsel
* Chain of Command
* Law Enforcement

With Unrestricted Report, knowledge of the sexual assault is limited to those with an official need-to-know.

In the event of an independent investigation that is initiated by a third party reporting from a source other than the victim. The victims can elect not to participate in the investigation by signing a 540k Victim Preference Letter. Speak to your SARC or SAPR VA for further information regarding the 540k Victim Preference Letter.

**Restricted Reporting** - is available for Service members and their SAPR eligible military dependents 18 years of age or older.

* Advocacy Services (support, information, referral, and accompaniment)
* Medical/Counseling Services
* Victims' Legal Counsel
* CATCH Program

A person who reported a sexual assault can choose to convert a Restricted Report to Unrestricted at any time.

One may still elect a Restricted Report if they did not personally report the sexual assault to law enforcement, including MCIOS, and/or did not previously elect to make an Unrestricted Report by signing a DD Form 2910 on the same sexual assault incident.

In the event a victim or third party discloses a Restricted Report to the command, it does not negate the command from the standard notification and reporting responsibilities.

For a **Restricted Report** - \*\* Some state and local laws require healthcare personnel to disclose sexual assault incidents to law enforcement. NDAA FY 16 Section 536 preempts mandatory reporting laws if the person reports to an MTF first, thereby preserving the Restricted Reporting option.

**Retaliation:**

The following individuals are eligible to report a retaliation in nexus to an Unrestricted Report to a SARC or SAPR VA via a signed DD Form 2910-2:

* Victims with an Unrestricted Report
* Adult sexual assault victim's adult family members
* Witnesses/Bystanders/1st Responders to include SARC and SAPR VAs

## Leaders Resources
As a leader, you may encounter a situation where there is a sexual assault in your unit.

Taking care of Marines is the plan of the day, every day. Doing it well requires constant training. The Marine Corps [Warfighter Mental Readiness Playbook](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=ab2955d1-7357-42a5-839b-282b3b018703&v=4) is a guide for effective influence.

**Command Leadership Responsibilities**

Per DoD policy, there are requirements that must be met to ensure the health and safety of survivors and to maintain unit cohesion through a positive command climate, if sexual assault occurs or is reported at your unit. [DoDI 6495.02](https://sapr.mil/policy) outlines in detail Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Program Procedures for the Department.

Service members have two reporting options: [Restricted and Unrestricted](https://sapr.mil/reporting-options). If a Service member discloses a sexual assault to law enforcement and/or previously elected to make an Unrestricted Report by signing a DD Form 2910 on the same sexual assault incident they are not eligible to make a Restricted Report. You can access the guide [Victim\_Reporting\_Options\_Guide (sapr.mil)](https://www.sapr.mil/?q=reporting-options) here.

Survivors of sexual assault shall be protected from coercion, retaliation, and reprisal in accordance with [DoDI 6495.02](https://sapr.mil/policy). Retaliation has no place in the military and you must do your part to ensure an ethical and just command intolerant of such behavior. For more information about retaliation, including reporting resources for survivors go to [Resources (marines.mil)](https://www.hqmc.marines.mil/igmc/Resources/).

To help ensure a comprehensive and appropriate response, DoD SAPRO has compiled a checklist of what should happen within the first 30 days of a survivor's disclosure of sexual assault. You can access the checklist [Commanders 30 Day Checklist | SAPR](https://www.sapr.mil/?q=toolkit-for-commanders-and-sarcs) here.

Throughout the military investigative and justice process, Service members who make an Unrestricted Report of sexual assault are entitled to certain rights. To learn more about these rights, please go to [Victims' Bill of Rights | SAPR](https://www.sapr.mil/victims-bill-rights).

**Tips on How to Talk to a Survivor**

Knowing what to say after a survivor has disclosed an assault can be difficult.

**"I'm so sorry this happened to you."** Showing a survivor empathy can build rapport and trust between you and the survivor.

**"I'm here to help you get support."** A survivor trusted you and shared what happened to them.

**"How can I help?"** Let the survivor know that you are there for them.

This is not a comprehensive list of what you can say to a survivor to show empathy. Commanders can find tips on what to say and what not to say to survivors of sexual violence in the Safe Helpline self-paced course, _How to Support a Survivor_, or by reviewing the information on this webpage.

**What is Safe Helpline?**

Established in 2011, [Safe Helpline](https://safehelpline.org/) is the Department of Defense's (DoD) sole hotline for members of the DoD community affected by sexual assault. Safe Helpline is a completely anonymous, confidential, 24/7, specialized service—providing help and information anytime, anywhere. A Safe Helpline user can access one-on-one support, peer-to-peer support, information, resources, and self-care exercises 24/7 to aid in their recovery.

**How Safe Helpline Can Support You and Your Unit**

[**Telephone Helpline**](https://www.safehelpline.org/telephone)

Our highly trained Safe Helpline staff are available to answer your questions, provide resources and get you contact information for a variety of on-base and off-base resources. You can connect with a staff member by calling [877-995-5247](tel:877-995-5247).

[**Online Helpline**](https://www.safehelpline.org/online)

The Online Helpline, an anonymous online platform, provides the same services as the Telephone Helpline described above. You can access the anonymous Online Helpline 24/7 by logging on to our website at [safehelpline.org](https://www.safehelpline.org/live-chat).

**Marine Corps Resources**

* [Inspectors General Checklist SEXUAL ASSAULT PREVENTION AND RESPONSE PROGRAM (SAPR) (1752)](https://www.igmc.marines.mil/Divisions/Inspections-Division/Functional-Area-Checklists-FACs/)
* [Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) Program Guidance](https://www.marines.mil/Portals/1/Publications/MCO%201752.5C.pdf?ver=2019-06-10-115714-627#:~:text=This%20Order%20establishes%20SAPR%20Program,those%20affected%20by%20this%20crime)

## Contact Information and Resources

pages.text:
# Substance Misuse

## SUBSTANCE MISUSE RESOURCES
HOW CAN WE HELP YOU?

**[800-662-HELP(4357)](tel:800-662-4357)**

## Signs of a Drinking Problem
Recognizing patterns takes awareness.

#### Changes in Body and Focus

* Needing to drink more to feel the same effect or to cope with stress, or difficulty concentrating.
* Noticeable decline in physical health, recurring hangovers, or trouble staying focused on daily tasks.

#### Friction in Relationships

* Pulling away from the unit, friends, or family in favor of drinking alone.
* Increased arguments or tension with the people who matter most to you.

#### Losing Your Way

* Finding yourself making choices that don't align with the person you want to be.
* A persistent feeling of being "stuck," losing hope, or feeling like your work lost its meaning.

#### Substance Misuse Assessment

If you recognize these signs in yourself, a loved one, or friend, connect with a professional for confidential, non-clinical guidance.

### Need help now? Support is available 24/7.

* [Immediate danger: Call 911](tel:911)
* Crisis line: Dial [988](tel:988) (press 1) or Chat Online: [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
* [SAMSHA Helpline: 1-800-662-4357](tel:18006624357)

## Regain Balance
Use these strategies to stay in control and reduce risks.

#### Control Your Environment

* Participate in activities that do not involve alcohol.
* Practice your "No" before heading out.

#### Set Your Limits

* Aim for no more than three standard drinks per occasion.
    * ➤ **Beer (5%):** 12 oz
    * ➤ **Wine (12%):** 5 oz
    * ➤ **Liquor (40%):** 1.5 oz
    * ➤ **Malt (7%):** 8 oz

#### Protect Your Why

* Keep your "why" visible on your phone as a consistent reminder of your priorities.
* Choosing environments and people that support your goals rather than testing your determination.

### Support Resources

You do not have to regain your balance by doing it alone. Connect with professional support:

* [Community Counseling Program](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling)
* [Family Advocacy Program](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/family-advocacy-program)
* [Chaplains](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/chaplains-religious-enrichment-development-operation)
* [Military and Family Life Counseling (MFLC)](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/resources/tools/mflc-locator)
* [OSCAR](https://manpower.usmc.afpims.mil/Divisions/Marine-and-Family-Programs/Marine-Corps-Total-Fitness-Directorate/#combat-power-preservation)
* [Other resources](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling)

Contact your local installation to inquire about services.

### Need help now? Support is available 24/7.

## Immediate Help and Support
You are not alone. Support is available 24/7.

#### Call 911

If you're in immediate danger or experiencing a crisis related to substance misuse, please call **911** or your local emergency services number.

#### SAMSHA National Helpline

Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMSHA) National Helpline:  
[1-800-662-4357](tel:18006624357)

#### 988 Lifeline or Veterans Crisis Line

* Call or Text: Dial [988](tel:988) and Press 1.
* Chat Online: [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
* Text: Send a message to [838255](sms:838255) or [988](sms:988)

#### Unit Support

* Chaplains
* OSCAR Team
* Substance Assessment Coordinator Officer

#### Military OneSource

[Confidential counseling](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-counseling/) provides service members and their loved ones with resources and support to address a variety of issues and build important skills to tackle life's challenges.

## Support Others
Your encouragement can be the turning point for a fellow Marine or loved one.

#### How to Start the Conversation

* **Be Direct:** Share specific behaviors you've noticed and why you are worried.
* **Express Care:** Ensure the person knows your concern comes from a place of support.
* **Offer Support:** Offer to go with the person to seek professional care.

#### Warning Signs of Medication Misuse

The DoD maintains a zero-tolerance policy for illicit substances.

* **Unauthorized Use:** Taking medication prescribed for someone else.
* **Incorrect Dosage:** Taking a larger dose or using it longer than prescribed.
* **Improper Administration:** Crushing, snorting, or injecting medication.
* **Unknown Substances:** Consuming any substance without knowing its exact contents.
* **Expired Medication:** Using old or expired prescriptions.

For more information, see [SECNAVINST 5300.28F.](https://www.secnav.navy.mil/doni/Directives/05000%20General%20Management%20Security%20and%20Safety%20Services/05-300%20Manpower%20Personnel%20Support/5350.4E.pdf)

Need help now? Support is available 24/7.

* [Immediate danger: Call 911](tel:911)
* Crisis line: Dial [988](tel:988) (press 1) or Chat Online: [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
* [SAMSHA Helpline: 1-800-662-4357](tel:18006624357)
* [Military OneSource: 1-800-342-9647](tel:18003429647)

## Leaders' Resources
Leaders, you are the first line of defense in maintaining the wellness and readiness of your units.

#### Foster a Healthy Culture

* **Lead by Example:** Demonstrate and encourage healthy coping mechanisms for stress, such as exercise and open communication, rather than turning to alcohol.
* **De-glamorize Alcohol:** Shift the focus away from alcohol at unit events and gatherings.

#### Know the Warning Signs

* **Performance:** Unexplained drop in work quality or tardiness.
* **Appearance:** Decline in personal hygiene or unkempt uniform.
* **Behavior:** Personality shifts, mood outbursts, or high-risk actions.

#### Combat Stigma

* **Engage with Empathy:** When you notice a Marine is struggling, engage with the individual in a supportive and non-judgmental manner, avoiding negative labels.
* **Challenge Stereotypes:** Actively challenge and correct negative stereotypes or inappropriate comments made about individuals with alcohol-related problems.
* **Promote Self-Referral:** Make it known that voluntarily help-seeking is a sign of strength and is designed to be career-safe.

#### Take Action

* **Refer for Screening:** Direct the Marine to a Substance Assessment and Counseling Center for professional assessment at the first sign of a problem.
* **Follow Up:** Continue to support and check in on the Marine.

#### Policies & Tools

#### Policies

* **DoDI 1010.04:** Establishes enterprise-wide substance misuse policy.
* **DoDI 1010.01 & 1010.16:** Directs military drug testing programs.
* **MCO 5300.17A:** Provides policy and procedural requirements for the Substance Assessment and Counseling Program (SACP)

#### Unit Support
