# Suicide Prevention

[](tel:988)

[TEXT: 838255](tel:838255)

[CHAT NOW](https://www.veteranscrisisline.net/get-help-now/chat/)

## HOW CAN WE HELP YOU?
[I need to talk to someone](https://www.veteranscrisisline.net/get-help/military-crisis-line)

[I have thoughts of suicide](#)

[I want to help someone else](#)

[Leaders resources](#)

[Prevention skills you can use](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/CMS_Themes/MCCS/resources/index.html)

## I'm Having Thoughts of Suicide
### Are You Thinking About Suicide?

If you are struggling or in pain, you don't have to face it alone.

**How to Connect:**

* **Call or Text:** Dial 988 and Press 1.
* **Chat Online:** [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
* **Text:** Send a message to 838255 or 988
* **Talk to Someone:** Reach out to your Chaplain or a trusted friend immediately.

### International Dialing (OCONUS)

If you are calling from a DSN phone, dial 988. If calling from off-base:

* **Northern Command:** Dial 988 then Press 1
* **Indo-Pacific Command:** +1 844-702-5493
* **European Command:** +1 844-702-5495
* **Central Command:** +1 855-422-7719
* **Africa Command:** +1 888-482-6054
* **Southern Command:** +1 866-989-9599

If you are OCONUS without a U.S. phone plan, use the online chat at [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat). These services are free, confidential, and available 24/7.

## Create a Safe Space
When you feel overwhelmed, your brain may tell you that things will never change.

**Secure Your Firearms**

Firearms are the most lethal method of suicide.

* **Off-site Storage:** Use your unit armory, a local gun shop, or a shooting range.
* **Lock It Up:** Use a cable lock or trigger lock and give the key to a trusted friend.
* **Ask for Help:** Contact your Suicide Prevention Program Coordinator (SPPC) or Officer (SPPO) for local options.

**Manage Medications**

Keep medications locked and safely dispose of unneeded pills using these methods:

* **The Bag Method:** Mix pills with coffee grounds or kitty litter in a sealed bag and throw it in the trash.
* **Drop-off Locations:** Take them to any military or local pharmacy. Find a location at [Safe.Pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/drug-disposal/).

**Identify Other Risks**

Think about your home.

## Unit Support
The Marines in your unit know what you're facing and are ready to help.

* **Chaplains:** 100% confidential support for any life challenge.
* **OSCAR Team Members:** Peer-to-peer support from fellow Marines trained to identify stress.
* **Mental Health Providers:** Direct clinical care within your medical network.
* **Resilience & Wellness Specialists:** Experts focused on mental fitness and proactive health.
* **Suicide Prevention Officers:** Your unit's primary contact for prevention resources.

## Community Support
You belong to a community of families and professionals dedicated to your resilience.

* **[Military & Family Life Counselors](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/benefits/military-family-life-counseling-program/):** For non-medical, confidential counseling.
* **[Community Counselors](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling):** Clinical counseling for individuals, couples, and families within the MCCS network.
* **[Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/):** 24/7 access to specialized support for all aspects of Marine Life.
* **[Semper Support](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/semper-support):** Free counseling sessions accessible from anywhere, on your schedule.

### MCCS is Here for You

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is committed to your well-being.

Connect to local base resources at [usmc-mccs.org](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/).

## I Want to Help Someone Else
If you believe a fellow Marine, friend, or loved one is in immediate danger, **do not leave them alone.** Please share the information below immediately:

**How to Connect:**

### International Dialing (OCONUS)

If you are calling from a DSN phone, dial 988. If calling from off-base:

If you are OCONUS without a U.S. phone plan, use the online chat at [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat).

## Step 1: Know the Signs
Trust your instincts and monitor for behavioral changes that often follow a challenging life event or loss.

**Listen for what the person says:**

* **Being a Burden:** "Everyone would be better off without me."
* **Hopelessness:** "There's no way out" or "I just want the pain to stop."
* **Finality:** Making statements about saying goodbye or talking about death (including dark humor).

**Watch for what the person does:**

* **Seeking Means:** Looking for firearms, pills, or other lethal items.
* **Withdrawal Socially:** Backing away from the unit, friends, or family.
* **Performance Drops:** Sudden decline in work, fitness, or personal hygiene.
* **Mood Shifts:** Extreme agitation or sudden, unexplained "calm."

## Step 2: Use the A.C.T. Tool
**Ask:** "How are you feeling?" ...

**Care:** Listen actively, with respect. No judgement. Let them know they're not alone.

**Take Action:** Secure lethal means. Connect them with mentors, leaders, and resources.

## Step 3: Share Support Resources
### Unit Support

* **Chaplains:** 100% confidential support.
* **OSCAR Team Members:** Peer-to-peer identification of stress.
* **Mental Health Providers:** Direct clinical care.
* **SPPC/SPPO:** Your unit's primary contact for prevention.

### Community Support

### MCCS is Here for You

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is committed to your well-being.

Connect to local base resources at [usmc-mccs.org](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/).

## Leaders Resources
### Seeking Help Is a Sign of Strength

As a leader, you play a critical role in educating your Marines and their families about suicide prevention and mental fitness. You must foster an environment where seeking help is seen as essential to maintaining readiness and well-being.

If you believe one of your Marines is in danger, **do not leave them alone.** Please share the information below immediately:

### The Military & Veterans Crisis Line

Free, confidential, and available 24/7 for Service members and their families.

**How to Connect:**

* **Call or Text:** Dial 988 and Press 1.
* **Chat Online:** [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) or [988 Lifeline](https://chat.988lifeline.org/)
* **Text:** Send a message to 838255 or 988

### International Dialing (OCONUS)

If you are calling from a DSN phone, dial 988. If calling from off-base:

If OCONUS without a U.S. phone plan, use the [Veterans Crisis Line](https://www.my.vavet.sites.va.gov/vclchat) online chat.

## Step 1: Identify Risk in Your Unit
Suicide and self-harm are often associated with stressors like relationship distress, work performance issues, pending legal actions, or transitions in duty status.

**Listen for what the person says:**

**Watch for what the person does:**

* **Seeking Means:** Looking for firearms, pills, or other lethal items.
* **Withdrawal Socially:** Isolation, backing away from the unit, friends, or family.
* **Performance Drops:** Sudden decline in work, fitness, or personal hygiene.
* **Mood Shifts:** Extreme agitation, reckless behavior, or unexplained "calm."
* **Digital Cues:** Posting self-destructive or hopeless content on social media.

**Command Individual Risk & Resiliency Assessment System (CIRRAS)**

Use the Marines Corps' official system of record to proactively identify and manage risk and resiliency factors.

* **Standardize Force Preservation:** Access transferable data on risk factors during PCS moves.
* **Inform Leadership Decisions:** Use real-time data to drive Force Preservation Councils (FPC).
* **Train Your Team:** Ensure subordinate leaders are proficient in using CIRRAS securely.

## Step 2: Use the A.C.T. Tool
**Ask:** "How are you feeling?" ...

Don't avoid the question. Don't be afraid of the answer.

**Take Action:** Secure lethal means.

## Step 3: Use Command Resources, Assets, and Support
**[The Warfighter Mental Readiness Playbook](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=ab2955d1-7357-42a5-839b-282b3b018703&v=4)**

Use this playbook to foster a culture where mental readiness is prioritized. It includes:

* **Effective Conversations:** Strategies for talking to Marines in need.
* **Mental Health Roadmap:** A clear path for navigating care and resources.
* **Commander Assets:** Tools to foster unit connection and well-being.

### Command Assets

* **Chaplains:** 100% confidential support for any life challenge.
* **OSCAR Team Members:** Peer-to-peer identification and stress management.
* **Mental Health Providers:** Direct clinical care within your medical network.
* **Resilience & Wellness Specialists:** Experts focused on mental fitness and social skill building.
* **SPPC/SPPO:** Your unit's primary contact for prevention resources and local safety.

### Community Support

* **[Military & Family Life Counselors](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/benefits/military-family-life-counseling-program/):** For non-medical, confidential counseling.
* **[Community Counselors](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling):** Clinical counseling within the MCCS network.
* **[Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/):** 24/7 access to specialized support for all aspects of Marine Life.
* **[Semper Support](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/semper-support):** Free counseling accessible from anywhere, on your schedule.

### MCCS is Here for You

Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is committed to your well-being.

Connect to local base resources at [usmc-mccs.org](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/).

Free, confidential, and available 24/7
Press 1 when calling 988

# Victim Advocacy Program

## Victim Advocacy
Victim Advocates provide information, guidance, and support to victims. They are specially trained to respond to incidents of domestic violence 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Victim Advocates provide emotional support; advise victims of their rights, explore resources and service in both civilian and military communities, and accompany and support victims through medical and legal proceedings.

Adult victims of domestic violence have two reporting options: Unrestricted and Restricted. Restricted Reporting allows adult victims to receive help without requiring notifications to law enforcement or command.

## Transitional Compensation
If you or someone in your family has been abused, Transitional Compensation can help you start a new life. This program provides 12-36 months of financial compensation and military ID card benefits and privileges to families of service members separated for domestic violence.

Main Side Office: 2034 Barnett Ave, Quantico VA 22134. 703-784-2570

Camp Barrett/TBS Office: 24009 Montezuma Ave, Quantico VA 22134. 703-432-6442
Monday-Friday 0730-1630 and Tuesday evenings until 1900.

For more information on the reporting options and support services available to military service members and spouses, please contact a Victim Advocate.

If you have an emergency, please call 911 immediately.

For after hours reporting of suspected child abuse or neglect, please contact the Virginia Child Abuse Hotline at 1-800-552-7096.

## Self Assesment for Relationship Violence
Do any of the following describe your current or past relationships?

1. My partner is extremely jealous or controlling. S/he accuses me of cheating or keeps me from
2. work/school/church/friends.
3. Sometimes I feel afraid or scared.

5. My partner physically fights me - hitting, pushing, or shoving.
6. My partner has strangled me.
7. My partner has forced me to have sex when I haven't wanted to.
8. I have done these things to my partner.

pages.text:
# Transition Readiness Program

We prepare Marines for the civilian workforce through the Transition Readiness Program by providing guidance and training for transitioning success.

## Steps to Success
### Step One: Individualized Initial Counseling

**Complete the Individualized Initial Counseling (IC) no later than 365 days prior to EAS date.**

- Contact your Unit Transition Coordinator (UTC) for IC pre-work instructions and assistance with scheduling IC with your installation's TRP office.

**IC pre-work requirements include:**

- Launching your DD Form 2648
- Registration on VA.gov
- Downloading your VMET and JST
- Completing the [NAVMC 17031](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=711553b5-5c26-4b47-baed-d30be328b0db&v=1)
- Review of the Pre-Separation Counseling Resource Guide
- Completion of the virtual Reserve Obligations and Opportunities Brief (ROOB)
- Update personal email address in MOL

[Download Checklist](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=ca147aec-39d7-40b9-969b-2306d09668f1&v=1)

### Step Two: Pre-Separation Counseling Brief

**Attend the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief no later than 365 days prior to your EAS date.**

- You must complete your IC before attending the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief.
- The Pre-Separation Counseling Brief is an in-person class which provides high level information on the many benefits, services, resources, and programs available during and after transition.
- Contact your UTC or TRP office for assistance with scheduling your attendance to the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief.

[Pre-Separation Counseling Resource Guide](https://www.tapevents.mil/Assets/ResourceContent/TAP/Pre_Separation_Counseling_Resource_Guide.pdf)

### Step Three: Transition Readiness Seminar Courses

**Attend the Transition Readiness Seminar (TRS) courses no later than 180 days prior to your EAS date.**

- You must complete the Individual Initial Counseling (IC) and attend the Pre-Separation Counseling Brief to register for the TRS courses.
- Contact your UTC for assistance with scheduling your attendance to the TRS courses.

### Step Four: Capstone Review

**Conduct Capstone Review no later than 120 days prior to your EAS date.**

- You must attend all the TRS courses before you can complete the Capstone Review.
- You and a TRP Advisor will review your completion of all mandated Career Readiness Standards (CRS) and discuss your transition plans.
- Your DD Form 2648 will be forwarded to your commander or commander's designee at the conclusion of Capstone Review.
- You must contact your UTC or TRP office to schedule your Commander's Verification.

### Step Five: Commander's Verification

**Complete Commander's Verification no later than 90 days prior to your EAS date.**

- You must complete the Capstone Review before the Commander's Verification.
- At Commander's Verification, your CO or designee will validate your overall preparedness to transition and will conduct any warm handovers to services or resources as needed based on your transition plan.
- Your CO or designee will digitally sign your DD Form 2648 at the conclusion of Commander's Verification.
- You will need to provide a copy of your completed and signed DD Form 2648 to your UTC.
- You will also need to provide a copy to IPAC in order to receive your DD214.

## Programs, Resources & Support
Get started on your steps for the Transition Readiness Seminar with a detailed checklist, documents, and downloads, preparing you for success as you begin your transition from military service to civilian life.

#### Getting Started

Your success transitioning from Military service to civilian life depends on you being proactive, persistent, and prepared.

- [Five Steps to Success](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=0fa4ff2b-c3d4-4fc6-ba04-07a407c941fd&v=1)

**Individual Initial Counseling Check List**

[Download Individual Initial Counseling Check List](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=ca147aec-39d7-40b9-969b-2306d09668f1&v=1)

**Tier Level Checklist**

- [Tier Level 1](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=0121e7e3-4e3b-4d02-b80b-933a11b5fdaf&v=1)
- [Tier Level 2](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=9e81f3c0-4252-4771-9afa-b564f5830baa&v=1)
- [Tier Level 3](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=b57de1c1-08f8-4432-a1c5-abad61f684bc&v=1)

**Participant Guide**

- Review Pre-Separation Counseling Resources
- Pre-Separation Counseling Guide
- Managing Your (MY) Transition
- Military Occupational Code (MOC) Crosswalk
- Employment Fundamentals of Career Transition
- VA Benefits & Services
- Employment Track: DOL Employment Workshop (DOLEW)
- DOL Career & Credential Exploration (C2E) Vocational
- Managing Your (MY) Education (MYEd)

[Download Participant Guide](https://www.tapevents.mil/resources/documents/)

**Downloads**

- [GAP Analysis](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=3aac04ae-0658-4878-9350-1fee464b4444&v=1)

## Direct Affiliation Program
Marines transitioning to the Marine Corps Reserve through the Direct Affiliation Program qualify for up to a $25K signing bonus, choice of duty station, and lateral move opportunities.

[Learn More](https://www.manpower.marines.mil/Manpower-Management/Enlisted-Assignments/Stay-Marine/Direct-Affiliation-Program/)

## SkillBridge
SkillBridge connects Marines to real job opportunities, offering training, apprenticeships, or internships for civilian work experience.

[Learn More](https://skillbridge.osd.mil/)

## Marine For Life Network
Marine For Life Network (M4L) connects transitioning Marines and their family members to education resources, employment opportunities, and other Veterans services that aid in their career and life goals outside of military service.

Learn More

## Personal Financial Management Program
A solid understanding of personal finances will prepare Marines and their family members for a successful transition from military service to civilian life - building confidence when facing financial challenges and responsibilities.

Learn More

# Marine For Life Network

We connect transitioning Marines, family members, and veterans to educational resources, employment opportunities, and services that support their career and life goals.

## Connect with a Regional Network Manager
Receive professional support and valuable information.

**I am a transitioning Marine...** wanting to connect to resources.

**I am a family member...** wanting to grow my network.

**I am a veteran...** wanting support and services.

**I am a military-friendly resource...** wanting to support and mentor Marines.

## Marine For Life Network Representatives
Supporting your journey from military service to civilian careers.

Marine For Life Network Representatives (M4L Reps) are dedicated to supporting transitioning Marines, veterans, and their families by connecting them to a strong network of military-friendly resources and opportunities.

With Marine Individually Mobilization Augmentee (IMA) Reservists strategically located across the country, M4L Reps offer expert guidance and support to help you navigate the shift from military to civilian life. Whether you're seeking career opportunities, educational resources, or community connections, M4L Reps are here to support your success every step of the way.

**Why Connect with a M4L Rep?**

1. **Personalized Networking Support** - Our M4L Reps offer one-on-one guidance to help you expand your professional network. By connecting you with local employers, veteran services, and community resources, they ensure you have the right tools and relationships to succeed in your new venture.

2. **Build Local Networks for Career Success** - Each M4L Reps builds and maintains a network of Marine-friendly employers, veteran services, and resources within 100-150 miles of their location.

3. **Mentorship and Leadership** - With a wealth of military and civilian career experience, M4L Reps can provide mentorship to help you navigate the challenges of civilian networking. Learn how to leverage your military background, build professional relationships, and enhance your career prospects in the civilian workforce.

4. **Monthly Networking Events** - M4L Reps hosts monthly networking events where Marines, veterans, and local community members can connect, share experiences, and explore career opportunities.

5. **Advocacy and Ongoing Support** - M4L Reps are committed to advocating for you throughout your transition and beyond military service.

6. **Building a Network for Success** - The Marine For Life Network (M4LN) isn't just about finding a job—it's about creating relationships that will support you in your career and beyond. By connecting you with the right people and resources, M4LN ensures you have access to the tools, knowledge, and connections needed to thrive in civilian life.

## Regional Industries Highlights
Exploring the unique opportunities each region has to offer.

As you transition from military service to civilian careers, each region of the U.S.

Below is a brief overview of the top industries in each region and how they might fit with your expertise.

**West** - The West Region is a prime location for tech careers, with Silicon Valley in California and tech centers in Washington offering plenty of opportunities. Veterans with skills in technology, management, or healthcare will find a wealth of career options in this region.

**Southeast** - In the Southeast Region, manufacturing is a key industry, especially in automotive, aerospace, and electronics in states like Alabama, South Carolina, and Georgia.

**Central** - The Central Region offers strong opportunities in manufacturing, particularly in automotive, steel, and machinery, with a focus in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana. Veterans with experience in these fields or looking to enter new sectors will find promising prospects here.

**Northeast** - The Northeast Region is a key hub for finance and insurance, with major centers in New York City and Boston. This area is ideal for veterans with backgrounds in finance, healthcare, education, technology, or government seeking new career paths.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find quick answers to commonly asked questions.

**What is the Marine for Life Network?**

The Marine for Life Network is a resource and support network designed to assist transitioning Marines, veterans, and their families with employment, education, and community reintegration.

**What services does the Marine for Life Network provide?**

The Marine for Life Network provides a variety of services, including career counseling, job search assistance, networking opportunities, educational resources, and connections to local community support.

**How can the Marine for Life Network help with my job search?**

The network connects you with employers who value military experience, provides resume and interview preparation assistance, and offers access to job fairs and networking events.

**Can I join the Marine for Life Network if I'm still on active duty?**

Yes, transitioning Marines can join the network while still active duty.

**Is there a cost to join the Marine for Life Network?**

No, the Marine for Life Network is a free resource available to Marines, veterans, and their families.

# SkillBridge

Connecting Marines to real job opportunities – offering training, apprenticeships, or internships for civilian work experience.

## Eligibility Requirements
Check to see if you are eligible to use SkillBridge.

Eligibility for participation in the SkillBridge includes:

* Active Duty Service Members

Participation in the SkillBridge program is not an entitlement and is at the commander's discretion based on the needs of the Marine Corps and mission requirements.

You are encouraged to attend the SkillBridge Information Session to learn how to successfully navigate through the SkillBridge program.

**Eligibility Requirements**

* Marines who have served a minimum of 180 days on active duty and received honorable discharge, including general discharge (under honorable conditions) within 180 days.
* Marines in the process of separating or retiring, must ensure adequate time remaining on contract prior to EAS by identifying their Category type, permitted timeline and final approval authorities for SkillBridge Program participation.
* Complete the Transition Readiness Seminar requirements at least 180 days before separation.
* Obtain command approval before participating in a Marine Corps SkillBridge program. Information on how to apply through your command will be provided during the SkillBridge Information Session.
* Marines enrolled in the Individual Disability Evaluation System or assigned to the Wounded Warrior Transition Program will require Commander consideration and approval of a SkillBridge Program packet and a separation date within 180 days.

**Timelines for SkillBridge Participation and Approval Authority**

The following indicates the maximum amount of time before your actual separation or retirement date that you can begin the program, pending the required approval from the appropriate authority.

* **Category I (E1-E5)**: up to 120 days, requires approval from Commanders at the grade of O5 or above.
* **Category II (E6-E7, WO-CWO3, O1-O4)**: up to 90 days, requires approval from Commanders at the grade of O5 or above.
* **Category III (E8-E9, W4-W5, O5 and above)**: up to 90 days or less, requires General Officer approval and Marine's SkillBridge participation must not result in a gapped billet.

**Program Policy and Guidance:**

* [NAVMC 1700.2B](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=612f26be-8283-4e0f-b1ee-244eb7143265&v=1)
* [MARADMIN: 280/24](https://www.marines.mil/News/Messages/Messages-Display/Article/3809908/interim-guidance-on-the-implementation-of-the-skillbridge-program/)
* [DoDI 1322.29](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=3eda3dd9-7736-40b2-8628-1f249d813189&v=1)

## Application Process
Learn how to successfully submit your SkillBridge application.

The application process may vary from installation to installation.

We encourage you to contact your SkillBridge coordinator and attend the SkillBridge Information Session before you process your application.

**Selection / Acceptance**
Applying does not guarantee your acceptance with a SkillBridge industry partner. Please adhere to the due dates and any additional information required.

**Your Responsibility**
You will be responsible for contacting the specific SkillBridge industry partner directly for information; a SkillBridge Coordinator will guide you through the application process. Authorization is obtained by uploading your packet and routing through NCMIS for final approval from your CO.

1. **Attend the SkillBridge Brief**
   Participate in the mandatory brief at your installation.

2. **Confirm Eligibility**
   Ensure you meet the eligibility criteria for the SkillBridge program.

3. **Command Approval**
   Discuss your interest in SkillBridge with your command to obtain their support.

4. **Check-Out/Separation Coordination**
   Connect with your local administrative office regarding check-out/separation procedures.

5. **Research SkillBridge Opportunities**
   Explore and apply to MOU-approved DoD SkillBridge organizations that match your career goals.

6. **Selection/Acceptance**
   Receive confirmation of your acceptance into a DoD-approved SkillBridge opportunity.

7. **Complete Application Packet**
   Gather and complete all necessary documents for the SkillBridge application.

8. **Submit for Review**
Submit your completed packet to your installation's SkillBridge office for review and conditional approval.

9. **Command Authorization**
   Submit your application through MyMarineEducation for final command authorization.

10. **Finalize Your Approval**
    Download and print your SkillBridge Approval Document from MyMarineEducation.

**Downloads**

[Sample Program Acceptance Letter](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=9e761b54-0f8c-44f2-961b-be46db9ecec5&v=1)

You must provide an acceptance letter for the program you are attending. The letter must include dates, times, location and a point of contact for the training.

## Information Session
Your first step to successfully navigating through SkillBridge.

We want to help you successfully transition into the civilian workforce by using the SkillBridge DoD-approved opportunities.

We encouraged you to attend the SkillBridge Information Session to learn essential details about the program:

* Eligibility Requirements
* Available DoD-Approved SkillBridge Opportunities
* How to Successfully Navigate the Application Process

During the session, you'll gain a comprehensive understanding of the program's requirements, timelines, and the commitment involved.

The session also offers a chance to ask questions, ensuring that you are fully informed before moving forward with any applications. Completion of the SkillBridge Information Session is required before you can engage with the program or submit any further documentation, making it a crucial step in your transition journey.

View the calendar section of this webpage or contact your local SkillBridge representative for session dates and times.

## SkillBridge Coordinators
Connect to a SkillBridge coordinator today!

Connect with SkillBridge coordinators to explore opportunities and receive guidance throughout your transition to civilian life.

If you are currently not located on a Marine Corps base, please contact the SkillBridge coordinator nearest to your location.

## Industry Training
Gain valuable hands-on experience through diverse training.

Industry training programs offer a chance for service members to gain industry-specific skills, certifications, and work experience through internships, apprenticeships, on-the-job training, and classroom instruction with approved civilian employers.

**Apprenticeship**

On-the-job training means learning both the hands-on and theoretical parts of a skilled job through a mix of practical experience and related lessons.

**Employment Skills Training**

Job skills training means training or education for job skills required by an employer to provide an individual with the ability to obtain employment.

**Internships**

A system of on-the-job-training offered by a JTEST-AI provider to eligible service members to develop jobs skills and employment skills training.

**On the Job Training**

A method of preparing teaching employees how to perform tasks by showing them, letting them try, and giving feedback.

**Pre-Apprenticeship**

Programs that offer an overview of trades, including qualifications, skills, and on-the-job-training and related instruction.

## DOW SkillBridge
Explore DOW-approved SkillBridge opportunities.

[www.skillbridge.mil](https://www.skillbridge.mil)

## Earn a Degree
Advance your education while serving!

Visit your Education Center and speak with a coordinator.

Voluntary Education

## Enroll in a University or College
Earn a degree after you transition from the Marine Corps.

The Leadership Scholar Program is a valuable resource for service members seeking to leverage their military experience into academic success and civilian career opportunities.

Service members interested in the Leadership Scholar Program should start by visiting the Volunteer Education and speaking to an education coordinator or the Transition Assistance Program coordinator.

Leadership Scholar Program

## Credentialing Opportunities Online
Your military skills and experience could provide you with credentials, certifications, and licenses.

The Credentialing Opportunities Program is an excellent way to leverage your military experience and prepare for a successful career both within the Marine Corps and in civilian life.

Marines interested in the COOL program should visit their local Volunteer Education Center and speak to an education coordinator to explore available credentials, understand the application process, and get started on obtaining valuable certifications and licenses.

[Credentialing Opportunities Online](https://www.cool.osd.mil/usmc/index.html)

## Budgeting for Your Future
Learn how to save and manage expenses during and after your transition.

We can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing expenses during and after your transition.

Personal Financial Management

## Managing Stress
Transitioning can be a complex and challenging process, both professionally and personally.

Establish a connection with professionals from your Community Counseling Program and discover a successful journey toward overcoming life's challenges.

Community Counseling

## FAQs
Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

**How do I verify which DOW SkillBridge organization I am eligible for?**

Marines may only participate with MOU-approved DOW SkillBridge organizations. Verify that participation will take place prior to the MOU-expiration date by identifying the MOU-expiration date by visiting, [www.skillbridge.mil/organizations](https://www.skillbridge.mil/organizations)

**Will I get paid during the SkillBridge program?**

Yes, service members continue to receive their military pay and benefits during the SkillBridge program, as they remain on active duty while participating in the program.

**Do I have to accept a job offer from the SkillBridge program?**

No, there is no obligation to accept a job offer from the SkillBridge program.

**Can SkillBridge participation delay my separation date?**

No, participation in SkillBridge does not delay your separation date.

**Can I relocate for a SkillBridge program?**

Yes, relocation for a SkillBridge program is possible, but it requires command approval and coordination. Any relocation costs are typically the responsibility of the service member unless otherwise arranged with the SkillBridge provider.

**Can I participate in SkillBridge while on terminal leave?**

No, SkillBridge participation is not allowed while on terminal leave. The program must be completed before starting terminal leave, as it is designed to be an active duty training opportunity.

**Is there a cost associated with SkillBridge?**

While the SkillBridge program itself is offered at no cost to service members, there are instances where industry partners may require the use of benefits like the GI Bill.

pages.text:
# Volunteer Opportunities

We connect you with meaningful volunteering opportunities that strengthen the military community and enhance the well-being of Marines and their families.

## Start Volunteering Today
Make a difference by giving your time, sharing your skills, and supporting the community.

## Eligibility
**Requirements:**

* Must be 13 years of age or older.
* Minors must have parental permission to volunteer.
* Must be willingly to offer, be accepted, and provide voluntary services.
* Must be in an off-duty status, if active duty or a civilian employee.
* Cannot count any fundraising activity as volunteerism.

## Getting Started
Getting started with volunteering is easy!

**Explore Volunteer Opportunities**

* Browse the volunteer webpage and calendar for available volunteer roles that match your interests and skills.

**Connect with the Volunteer Office**

* Contact the Volunteer Coordinator for more information about specific opportunities and application processes.

**Complete a Volunteer Application**

* Fill out the volunteer application form, providing necessary details such as your availability, interests, and any prior experience.

**Orientation or Training Session**

* Attend the required orientation or training to familiarize yourself with the program, expectations, and guidelines.

**Complete Background Check (if applicable)**

* For certain roles, especially those working with children or sensitive information, a background check may be required.

**Get Assigned**

* After your application is approved, you'll be matched with a volunteer position that suits your skills and interests.

**Begin Volunteering!**

* Start your volunteer journey, making a positive impact on your community while gaining valuable experience.

## Why Volunteer?
Volunteering offers many benefits, from personal growth and skill development to making meaningful connections and giving back to the community.

**Volunteering Benefits:**

* Community support
* Develop lasting relationships
* Enhances resumes
* Grow networks
* Personal growth and development
* Professional development
* Receive on-the-job training
* Teen volunteer opportunities
* Work flexible hours

**Life Skills Developed:**

* Communication
* Empathy and Compassion
* Strengthening Relationships
* Leadership
* Personal and professional development
* Problem-solving
* Networking
* Teamwork
* Time management

**Honorable Recognition:**

* Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal (MOVSM)
* President's Volunteer Service Award (PVSA)
* Volunteer Service Award (VSA)

## Volunteer Opportunities
Discover resources in your community.

## L.I.N.K.S
Lifestyle Insights, Networking, Knowledge, and Skills

The L.I.N.K.S.

**Curriculum Includes:**

* Our Corps, Our Culture
* Events & Etiquette
* Navigating Resources
* Pay & Entitlements
* Deployments
* Safe and Sound All Around
* The Place You Will Go
* Building Your Network
* Investing in Your Community
* Kids Readiness
* Mentor Training

**Volunteer!**

Are you wanting to make a difference in the lives of military families?

Learn more about L.I.N.K.S. by visiting Marine Corps Family Team Building.

## Single Marine Program
Volunteering with the Single Marine Program (SMP) supports the community, events, and helps enhance the quality of life for Marines and their families.

The Single Marine Program offers a wide variety of volunteer opportunities each month with flexible times, days, and locations to meet the needs of our diverse community.

Volunteer opportunities are available for single and geo-bachelor Marines.

Learn more about the volunteering opportunities through the Single Marine Program.

## Marine Corps Family Team Building
Volunteering with Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) empowers and supports Marine families through workshops, events, and vital resources that strengthen resilience and readiness.

MCFTB provides opportunities for training and volunteerism with L.I.N.K.S.

**L.I.N.K.S. Volunteers**

If you are interested in becoming part of the L.I.N.K.S. team, call us or visit our office for more information.

* Host/Greet at Sessions
* Food Angel – Help to Feed our Participants.
* Administrative Support
* Present L.I.N.K.S. Session Topics
* Information Booth Support
* Event Support

**UPFRP Volunteers**

Family Readiness Volunteers are an integral part of the UPFRP.

Connect with your DRC or URC and discover volunteer opportunities through Marine Corps Family Team Building.

## Coach Youth Sports
Volunteering for youth sports is a fantastic way to inspire young athletes while fostering teamwork, discipline, and a love for physical activity.

* Tee-Ball
* Baseball
* Basketball
* Flag Football
* Soccer
* Track

Not all sports listed are available at all locations.
Explore volunteer opportunities with [Youth Sports](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/recreation-fitness/sports/youth-sports).

## Base Schools
Marines and their families have valuable opportunities to volunteer at schools located on Marine Corps bases, contributing positively to the educational environment and fostering community engagement.

Here's how you can get involved:​

* Explore Volunteer Opportunities
There are a variety of volunteer opportunities that connect military personnel, their families, retirees, veterans, and civilians with local schools.

**Benefits of Volunteering**
Volunteering provides numerous advantages, including:

* Personal Growth: Develop new skills and gain experiences that can enhance personal and professional growth.​
* Community Connection: Strengthen ties within the military community by supporting local schools and educational programs.​
* Recognition: Eligible volunteers may receive awards such as the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Award or the President's Volunteer Service Award.

**Volunteer Roles**
Volunteer roles in base schools can vary but often include:

* Classroom Assistance: Supporting teachers with instructional activities and classroom management.​
* Tutoring: Providing one-on-one or small group academic support to students.​
* Extracurricular Activities: Assisting with clubs, sports, and other after-school programs.

**Initiate the Application Process**
To begin volunteering:

* Contact the Volunteer Coordinator: Reach out to the Installation Volunteer Coordinator at your base to express interest and learn about available opportunities.
* Complete Necessary Forms: Fill out the required volunteer application forms, which may include background checks and other necessary documentation.​

**Commit to a Schedule**

* Determine a volunteer schedule that aligns with your availability and the needs of the school. Consistency is often appreciated, but many programs offer flexibility to accommodate varying schedules.​

**Maintain Communication**

* Stay in regular contact with the school's volunteer coordinator to ensure a positive and effective volunteer experience.​

Not all installations offer volunteer opportunities with base schools.

## Navy Marine Corps Relief Society
The Navy Marine Corps Relief Society (NMCRS) is accepting professional volunteers to assist service members and eligible family members.

**Volunteer requirements:**

* Must have base access
* Be available between Monday through Friday from 8 a.m.-4 p.m.

**Volunteer opportunities include:**

* Client services - reception duties
* Casework - providing one-on-one financial education and assistance
* Budget for Baby - teaching workshops to military families expecting a child
* Well Baby Clinic - working with our visiting nurses to administer health checks and clothing exchange

All volunteers will be properly trained to support and assist with confidence.

Learn more about volunteer opportunities at the [Navy Marine Corps Relief Society](https://www.nmcrs.org/).

## Honoring Our Volunteers
We honor the outstanding commitment to volunteer service.

## Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal
The Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal is for members of the armed forces and reserve components. Service members will want to volunteer in their civilian and military communities for normally a period of three years, which do not need to be consecutive years.

Learn more about the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal by contacting the Volunteer Coordinator.

## Behind the Camouflage Spouse and Community Awards
The Marine Corps Association is excited to announce the launch of the **Behind the Camouflage Awards Program** to highlight the exceptional work Marine Corps spouses and community members are doing within their communities.

There are three opportunities to nominate spouses and community members who contributed to building the community and driving positive change.

**Spouse Spotlight**
Celebrating Marine Corps Spouses who excel in building community and driving positive change. Do you know an amazing Marine Corps Spouse who is an everyday hero working tirelessly behind the scenes to improve our community?

Nominate a spouse today at [Spouse Spotlight](https://www.mca-marines.org/btc-spouse-spotlight/)!

**Changemaker**
The Changemaker of the Year Award honors individuals who have made a significant, tangible impact within the Marine Corps community. This award recognizes those who have driven meaningful change by identifying challenges and implementing solutions that positively affect the lives of Marine Corps families, spouses, and the broader community.

Learn about eligibility and requirements, and nomination process at [Changemaker](https://www.mca-marines.org/community-change-maker/).

**Community Catalyst**
The Community Catalyst of the Year Award recognizes a member of the Marine Corps community who has shown exceptional dedication to building and nurturing a supportive environment.

Learn about eligibility, requirements, and nomination process at [Community Catalyst](https://www.mca-marines.org/community-catalyst/).

## How do I sign up to volunteer?
You can sign up by visiting the Volunteer office, contacting a volunteer coordinator, or checking the MCCS website for available opportunities and application instructions.

## What types of volunteer opportunities are available?
MCCS offers a wide range of opportunities, including roles in youth sports, the Single Marine Program, special events, and community support.

## Do I need prior experience or training to volunteer?
While some positions may require specific skills or training, many volunteer opportunities offer on-the-job training and welcome individuals of all experience levels.

## How do I track my volunteer hours?
Volunteer hours are typically tracked through sign-in sheets, volunteer logs, with verification by a coordinator or supervisor.

## Can I earn awards or recognition for my volunteer service?
Yes, volunteers may be eligible for awards such as the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal, the President's Volunteer Service Award, and other local or organizational recognition.

# Fitness

The Barber Physical Activity Center (BPAC) is a 57,000 square foot, state-of-the-art facility that houses Physical Fitness, Health Promotion, Athletics, and Single Marine Program. The facility offers a large variety of recreational opportunities with a 9,600 square foot fitness deck, group exercise room, spin studio, functional fitness room, three racquetball courts, and one full sized basketball court. It also offers a TV and Wi-Fi lounge, locker rooms, and separate saunas for men and women for all eligible patrons. Children 12-15 years old must be accompanied by an adult over 18. 16 and older are permitted unaccompanied access. 10–15-year-olds may use the basketball and racquetball courts when accompanied by an adult. Children under the age of 10 are not permitted access to the facility unless it is an organized MCCS or Command event open to all ages. ID is required for access to the facility, DoD civilians and Base Contractors.

## Unmanned Fitness Center
**Authorized Users: Active Duty Military, MCINCR-MCBQ PMO Civilians, and Fire Department personnel only.**

• Unmanned hours start 30 minutes after closing of regular hours: All patrons must exit facility.
• Unmanned access is turned off 30 minutes before opening: Patrons do not need to exit facility.
• Federal Holidays BPAC is open for unmanned access registrants only.

## Parking
Parking is available at BPAC and is adjacent parking lots across the street at Barnett Field and next to Butler Stadium.

## Policies
All patrons must present proper identification to enter BPAC. 100% ID check. Exception: Active Duty in uniform (this does not include PT uniform green-on-green). Patrons are required to present their IDs to the customer service front desk staff and log in on the touch screen to identify eligibility.

## Fees
Contractors working aboard MCB Quantico may access BPAC for a Daily Fee - $5.00 or Monthly Fee - $40.00.

Monthly Locker Fee - $15.00

(Available for DoD, Retirees, Family Members, and Contractors assigned to MCB Quantico.)

## Physical Fitness Program
The Quantico Physical Fitness Program is located in the Barber Physical Activity Center, Building 2073, Barnett Avenue. The Physical Fitness Program supports the Marine Corps PFT, CFT and weight control requirements. For more information on the Physical Fitness program, contact the Fitness Director at 703-784-2672.

# High Intensity Tactical Training

The primary purpose of the High Intensity Tactical Training (HITT) program is to enhance operational fitness levels and optimize combat readiness and resiliency for the Marine.

**ALL Hours are subject to change to meet the needs of the HITT Program.** Please check the website or call the HITT Coordinator for the most up to date information.

**HITT Instructor Led Sessions**

Open to all active duty or reservist ONLY. Daily HITT sessions will allow Marines, Reservists, and other Active Duty Personnel the opportunity to train in a highly motivated group setting.

**HITT UNIT PT Reservations**

The HITT Center can accommodate individual unit PTs led by our HITT Instructors upon approval from the HITT Coordinator. MCB Quantico offers a shadowing program which allows all HITT Level-1 and 2 instructors to utilize the facility for their units outside of MCCS operating hours. This also requires prior approval by the installation HITT Coordinator.

**ALL RESERVATONS MUST BE MADE AT LEAST 10 DAYS IN ADVANCE**

**Open Gym**

Patrons unable to attend an instructor led HITT session can train during posted open gym hours.

\*\*MARINES PARTICIPATING IN HITT HAVE PRIORITY OVER EQUIPMENT AND SPACE IN THE HITT CENTER AND IS SUBJECT TO THE INSTRUCTOR'S DISCRETION\*\*

# Personal Training

Jump start your exercise program with the help of a personal trainer.

## One-on-One Personal Training Sessions
No fees assessed for Active Duty on BCP or Reconditioning Program. Proper documentation required.

**Active Duty & Reservists**
3 one-on-one sessions with 1 Microfit assessment- Free
Additional sessions- $20 each (5 sessions $85)

**Family Members & Retirees**
3 one-on-one sessions with 1 Microfit assessment- $60
Additional sessions- $25 each (5 sessions $115)

**DoD Civillians**
3 one-on-one sessions with 1 Microfit assessment- $90
Additional sessions- $40 each (5 sessions $185)

**Contractors**
3 one-on-one sessions with 1 Microfit assessment- $100
Additional sessions- $50 each (5 sessions $225)

## Microfit Assessments
Using state of the art technology, receive a complete personalized fitness/lifestyle assessment. For appointments call 703.432.0593.

## Steps to Start Your Personal Fitness Program
If you have any of the following conditions, you will first need a [clearance form](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=996ea148-9684-4b56-a01b-2d5b3355d1dc) signed by your physician.

* Heart problems, chest pain, history of stroke
* High blood pressure, lung or breathing problems
* Men over age 45, women over age 55
* Diabetes, thyroid condition, high cholesterol
* Smoker, sedentary or any condition that would be aggravated by exercise
* If the above conditions do not exist in your health history, stop by BPAC to purchase and schedule your first Fitness Assessment, or call 703.432.0593.

After you hand carry, mail, or fax the Physician's Clearance form to your physician...

* Return the completed form in person or by fax to:
* Barber Physical Fitness Activities Center
* Attn: Physical Fitness
* 2073 Barnett Ave., Quantico, VA 22134
* Fax: 703.432.0588
* When the form is completed and returned, call or stop by BPAC and schedule an assessment with a Personal Trainer.
* Call 703.432.0593 between 0500-2000, Monday-Friday. 0800-1700 Sat/ 0900-1700 Sun.
* Workout appointments available 0530-1900 Mon-Fri/ 0830-1530 Sat/ 0930-1530 Sun.

# Health & Wellness Education

## Our Mission
The goal of Health Promotion is to improve the health and well-being, and to mitigate risk factors for the members of our community by enhancing readiness through the voluntary adoption of a healthy lifestyle.

## Classes
The Semper Fit Health Promotion program offers a variety of classes to provide education and support to keep you healthy.

* Tobacco Cessation
* Sexual Health
* Nutrition Education and Dietary Supplements
* Weight Management
* Physical Activity
* Injury Prevention
* Chronic Disease Prevention

All classes can be provided to the unit at BPAC or their location upon request.

## Event Support
Do you want to include health education on any of these topics for a class or at an event?

## Individual Nutrition Counseling
The Semper Fit Dietitian helps individuals reach their health goals. **Counseling sessions are available by appointment only.**

* Active Duty: Free
* Dependents. Reservists, and Retirees: $25 (Dependents must be 12+ years of age).
* DoD Civilians: $40
* Contractors: $50

## Monthly Nutrition Class
This free, one hour course is offered the 1st Wednesday of every month at 11:30 am - 12:30 pm at the link below via Adobe Connect:

* [Join](https://meeting.marinenet.usmc.mil/mcbqnutritionclass/) the meeting!

## Cooking Classes
* Cooking classes are offered quarterly.

## Healthy Grocery Store Tour
* Tours are offered by appointment for a group of three or more at the Quantico Commissary.

## Nutrition Briefs
* Health Promotion will come to you! Nutrition and health briefs are available to all units and civilian offices aboard Quantico.

## Free Health Screenings (Walk-in or By Appointment)
* Blood Pressure
* Body Composition via InBody
* Bone Density

## Tobacco Cessation
* Semper Fit Health Promotion has a standardized, evidenced-based tobacco cessation program called Operation Tobacco Free Marine (OTFM) which is free and open to all ID holders. The program launched in 2017, and we offer 1:1 counseling sessions by appointment.

## Sexual Health
* Our staff utilizes resources by the Navy and Marine Corps Public Health Center's Sexual Health and Responsibility Program (SHARP).

## Physical Activity and Injury Prevention
We partner with our Semper Fit Physical Fitness department to tailor classes to meet your audience's needs.

Contact: Health Promotion
Address: Building 2073 Barnett Ave, Quantico, VA 22134
Phone: 703-784-2869

- Monday–Friday: 7:30am - 4:00pm

# Golf Course

The Medal of Honor Golf Course proudly offers year-round golf on our 18-hole championship golf course. The course is open year-round to Active Duty and Retired Military, DoD civilian employees, family members, FBI Academy, National Guard and Reserve personnel, as well as the public.

[Book A Tee Time](https://www.chronogolf.com/club/medal-of-honor-golf-course)

## Course History
The Medal of Honor Golf Course, originally called The Officers' Club Golf Course, began in 1930 as a six-hole layout, most likely built by Marine Corps construction personnel. The course grew to 9-holes, with two tee boxes on each hole, around 1934. The course expanded again to 18-holes in the mid-1940s and became known as the Quantico Golf Course. This growth was led by Ernest Stanley, who was the Golf Course Superintendent from 1933 to 1976. In 1980, the Quantico Golf Course was renamed the Medal of Honor Golf Course in honor of Marines who have earned the nation's highest medal for valor.

## Swing Lab
Take your play to the next level.

* **Rental Policy** – Tee up a round of golf with friends or dial in your game with a practice session. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your tee time.
* **Club Fitting** – PGA Professional Master Certified Fitters measure and benchmark your current clubs, then provide new combinations of club heads and shafts to hit, dialing in the perfect equipment for your swing using metrics provided by our state-of-the-art E6 launch monitor data.
* **Swing & Video Analysis** – Swing Catalyst Software & thermographic weight tracking pressure mat technology is used for slow motion viewing, and frame by frame analysis of your golf swing.
* **High Tech Swing Evaluation** – K Coach Certified PGA Professionals use the K-VEST wearable motion biofeedback learning system to augment and enhance verbal instruction to accelerate the pace of improvement.
* **Golf Lessons** – Improve your golf game with simulator golf lessons, choose from High Tech, Adult, Junior, or Winter Maintenance.
* **Golf Improvement Package** – If you are ready to take your game to the next level, our golf improvement package is just the thing, this package includes a High Tech lesson, two indoor lessons and five hours of simulator practice time.
* **Six Month Simulator Subscription** – Take advantage of our flexible six-month simulator subscription plan.

## Tee Times
The Medal of Honor Golf Course offers an online tee time system based on a priority system.

* Initial registration will default first time users to the General Public category. The priority system protects our Active-duty military personnel's right to first access.
* Active-duty military can book tee times up to ten days in advance.
* Members can book tee times up to nine days in advance.
* Retired Military/Veterans/DoD can book tee times up to eight days in advance.
* General Public can book tee-times up to seven days in advance.
* [Book A Tee Time Online](https://www.chronogolf.com/club/medal-of-honor-golf-course)

**Proper attire required: Collared shirts & Bermuda shorts/skirts.**

**MCBO 1700.2A**

Youth Golf

a. Children under seven (7) years of age are not permitted on the Golf Course, unless playing in our Youth Golf Program, i.e., First Tee Program, with signed parental consent.

# Lunga Park

Marine Corps Base Quantico and Marine Corps Community Services have been working tirelessly over the past several years to rebuild and reopen this facility for you and your family's enjoyment.

Lunga Park is open 7 days a week, sunrise to sunset. Rentals are only available during Boathouse hours. Pets are allowed but must remain on a leash.

Per DoD policies, only authorized patrons (and guests) of MWR may be permitted access to Lunga Park in accordance with base access policies.

**The following individuals have full access to MWR services and programs:**

* Active-duty service members and their families
* Members of the National Guard and reserves and their families
* Current and retired DoD civilian employees
* Service academy and Merchant Marine cadets
* Retired service members and their families
* Honorably discharged veterans with a 100% service-connected disability
* Medal of Honor recipients
* Surviving family members of uniformed service members or retirees until they age out of eligibility or their dependent status associated with the deceased member or retiree changes

Please refer to the [MCBQ Visitor Control Center](https://www.quantico.marines.mil/Info/Base-Access/Visitor-Control-Center/) for any base access questions.

## Go Play
* All rentals and reservations of picnic sites, pavilions, tent sites, cabin rentals, and the beach volleyball court will be conducted from the Lunga Boathouse on a first-come, first served basis.
* All rental gear such as watercraft, tents, coolers, camping and fishing gear will be conducted at the Boathouse and will follow the same pricing guidelines as the out-door recreation gear issue that the Marina has in place. Pricing is listed in the park information and fees brochures and flyers.
* Pets allowed but must be on a leash at all times.

For more information, check out our [FAQ's](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=28621ab4-59dc-4498-8453-e58b9b9cca3a&v=1).

## Go Camp
Camp Site Rentals:

* Tent Sites - $25 per night.
* Rustic Cabin - $40 per night (two nights minimum)

## Go Fish
* All patrons wanting to fish should refer to MCINCR-MCBQO 11015.2D Fish and Wildlife Management Manual and regulations found at [https://quantico.isportsman.net](https://quantico.isportsman.net/).
* Bait will be available from the Lunga Park General Store during store operating hours.

**Fishing Hours of Operation**
(subject to change)

Monday-Sunday: 30 minutes before sunrise -- 30 minutes after sunset

## Go Safe
Check out our [safety brochure](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=c8b84874-3b5b-4bd5-99d3-cb7dd2776bc1&v=1).

## Go Boat
* All Virginia Boaters Safety rules apply to personally owned boats, see: [https://dwr.virginia.gov/boating/boaters-guide/](https://dwr.virginia.gov/boating/boaters-guide/)
* Virginia Requirements regarding Personal Flotation Devices (PFD) can be found at: [https://www.boat-ed.com/virginia/studyGuide/Specific-PFD-Requirements/10104702_49798/](https://www.boat-ed.com/virginia/studyGuide/Specific-PFD-Requirements/10104702_49798/)
* Patrons will be able to launch boats (with the exception of June 3) during launch operating hours only.
* Personally owned watercraft must obtain a launch pass from the Lunga Boathouse PRIOR TO LAUNCH.
* All boaters and paddlers must sign in to isportsman at **[https://quantico.isportsman.net](https://quantico.isportsman.net/)**.
* **No gas boating allowed.** Boats that have gas engines can be used, however, the engine must be raised and not utilized. If the boat has a removable fuel cell, the cell must be removed from the vessel prior to launching.
* **Personal watercraft (Jet Skis) or paddle boards are NOT PERMITTED in Lunga Reservoir.**
* No anchoring of any kind is allowed in Lunga Reservoir.
* No Swimming or Wading is allowed within Lunga Reservoir.
* Marina personnel have the right to refuse boat usage to anyone who, in their opinion, is not competent to sail, operate a powerboat, or who smells of alcohol or appears to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. See MCBO 1700.2.
* No individual is to store, dispense, or consume alcoholic beverages in any buildings under the control of the Harbormaster. Patrons may consume beer only at the picnic areas. These restrictions do not apply to patrons on private boats.
* MCCS personnel, at their discretion, may at any time delay or cancel boat usage due to existing or projected inclement weather, i.e.. gusty winds, thunderstorms, or steady winds in excess of 16 knots.

**Boathouse Hours of Operation**
(subject to change)

Labor Day - Memorial Day: Monday-Sunday, 7:00am - 3:00pm

Memorial Day - Labor Day:
* Monday - Thursday: 7:00am - 3:00pm
* Friday - Sunday: 7:00am - 7:00pm

## Go Paddle
* MCCS rental watercraft will be issued from the Lunga Boathouse on a first-come, first served basis only. **Rentals are only available during Boathouse hours.**
* All MCCS powered watercraft will be operated by electric motor only by base order.
* Personal Flotations Devices (PFDs) must be worn at all times.
* Alcoholic beverages will not be permitted on MCCS watercraft at any time.
* No anchoring of any kind is allowed in Lunga Reservoir.
* No swimming or wading is allowed within Lunga Reservoir.
* MCCS personnel, at their discretion, may at any time delay or cancel boat usage due to existing or projected inclement weather, i.e.. gusty winds, thunderstorms, or steady winds in excess of 16 knots.
* Marina personnel have the right to refuse boat usage to anyone who, in their opinion, is not competent to sail, operate a powerboat, or who smells of alcohol or appears to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs. See MCBO 1700.2.
* No individual is to store, dispense, or consume alcoholic beverages in any buildings under the control of the Harbormaster. Patrons may consume beer only at the picnic areas. These restrictions do not apply to patrons on private boats.

**Boathouse Hours of Operation**
(subject to change)

Labor Day - Memorial Day: Monday-Sunday, 7:00am - 3:00pm

Phone: 703-784-5270

# Marinas & Boating

The Quantico Marina is located just past the town of Quantico at the end of Potomac Avenue. We have 150 wet slips that can accommodate vessels 14 to 50 feet in length. The Marina has a fuel dock with 89 octane unleaded pump out station and small convenience store with ice, drinks, and snacks. Boat rentals are available 15 May – 15 October. If you are renting a boat, please call ahead for weather conditions. Children must be six years old to be passengers on any rental boat.

## Services
- Private berthing
- Dry Storage
- Resale
- Resources and services are available to Marines and families.
- Programs designed to enhance and promote the mental and physical well-being of Service members and considered essential to sustaining readiness.

The Quantico Marina is located just past the town of Quantico at the end of Potomac Avenue. We have 150 wet slips that can accommodate vessels 14 to 50 feet in length.

If you are renting a boat please call ahead for weather conditions. Children must be 6 years old to be passengers on any rental boat. (Refund for weather or mechanical issues only.)

Virginia requires all motorboat operators to take Certified Boat Safety Course. Please visit Virginia Department of Game & Inland Fisheries website at www.dgif.virginia.gov/boating or call 804-367-1000 for class schedules.

Anglers age 16 and older fishing these waters must have in their possession a Virginia freshwater fishing license per Virginia fishing regulations, available online at www.dgif.virginia.gov/fishing. pages.text:
# All-Marine Sports

All-Marine Sports provides elite Marine athletes the opportunity to compete in higher level competitions to include Armed Forces Championships, National Championships, Conseil International du Sport Militaire (CISM) Championships, and the Olympics.

## Coaching Opportunities
Support elite Marine athletes as coaches and mentors.

Whether you're a passionate coach looking to shape the next generation of Marine athletes or a competitor driven to perform at the highest level, All-Marine Sports is seeking dedicated individuals who embody the Marine Corps values of Honor, Courage, and Commitment. Submit your application to [AllMarineSports@usmc-mccs.org](mailto:AllMarineSports@usmc-mccs.org) today and answer the call where preparation meets opportunity.

## Standard Test Events
Scores for the following events are required by applicants.

Click on the event name for more information and how to correctly perform the event.

#### Running

Most current running times for:

## Additional Opportunities
Opportunities for elite athletes to compete in sports.

#### Athletes of the Year

The Marine Corps is searching for its top Marine athletes. Marines who have excelled in intramural, varsity, All-Marine, national, and international competitions will be considered for the 2025 Male and Female Athletes of the Year.

Competitions must comply with the amateur regulations within nationally recognized governing bodies or affiliated organizations within the US Olympic Committee. Applications must include a professional biography encompassing the Marine's calendar year accomplishments in the sport and professional Marine Corps background.

Athletes must provide published or final results, such as time and scores associated with the sport the applicant participated in within the 2025 calendar year. Please [download the application](/modules/media/?do=download&id=1a96d68c-3a2a-4f18-92d4-67efc3d231df&v=1&v=1) and email the completed form to [AllMarineSports@usmc-mccs.org](mailto:AllMarineSports@usmc-mccs.org).

All applications are due to HQMC Semper Fit no later than February 16, 2026. The applicant's commanding officer (O5 level Command or higher) must endorse the application.

#### U.S. Armed Forces Sports

The Armed Forces Sports (AFS) program was officially established in 1948 as the Inter-service Sports Council (ISSC). The AFS program offers 25 men and women team and individual sports; annually conducts 16 Armed Forces Sports Championships and 9 qualifying events/Trial Camps; participates in 9 U.S. national championships and 16 CISM Military World Championships. Visit the [AFS website](http://armedforcessports.defense.gov/About/).

#### Conseil International du Sport Militaire (CISM)

CISM is the second largest multi-sport discipline organization after the International Olympic Committee. They represent the highest level of military athletic competitiveness and organize various sporting events for the Armed Forces of their 136 member countries.

## Applications
Submit your completed application to compete as an elite athlete.

NOTE: Applications MUST be viewed in Adobe Acrobat. It will not be viewable in a web browser.

**All-Marine Sports Application**

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Quick answers to common questions.

#### Athletic Directors

**Q: What policy governs All-Marine Sports?**

A: DoD Directive 1330.4 allows Marines to participate in Armed Forces, National, and International sports activities.

**Q: Who is eligible for the All-Marine Sports Program?**

A: The total force, with the exception of Inactive Ready Reservist (IRR), are eligible to participate on All-Marine Sports teams (active duty and active reserve). Reservist must be placed on orders (ADOS/similar) by their command to participate and receive TAD funds for travel from HQMC.

**Q: Who pays for the TAD?**

A: HQMC All-Marine Sports will fund all travel (flights/rentals/lodging/meals and incidentals) for Trial Camps, Armed Forces and higher level competition.

**Q: What happens if a Marine is selected to an All-Marine Trial Camp?**

A: All-Marine Sports generates a selection message and sends it to each Marine selected. Each Marine will be responsible for creating their DTS authorization and signing it so that All-Marine Sports can approve the travel. Government Travel Card use is mandatory for required travel and centrally billed accounts will not be authorized.

**Q: What if my Commander needs a Marine back early from an All-Marine Sports competition?**

A: If the Commander needs a Marine back early for mission requirements, the All-Marine Sports Office will attempt to make travel arrangements to have the Marine back within 24 hours. This return cost may be the responsibility of the command.

**Q: If selected will a Marine receive PCS orders or change of MOS?**

A: This is a short term Temporary Assigned Duty (TAD) opportunity (4 days to 2 months depending on the sport and your selection for higher competitions).

**Q: When will Marines be notified to "Try Out"?**

A: Selections will be made to attend Trial Camp from the information provided in the applications and contacting references. Notifications will be made approximately two (2) weeks following the application deadline through a selection message. Marines must be in peak physical condition to compete immediately.

**Q: What do Marines need to bring to Trial Camp?**

A: Specific requirements for each Trial Camp vary by sport and location. The head coach will reach out to the Marines selected prior to travel and provide a list of required items. In addition, each Marine is required to bring a pair of khaki pants, belt, and dress shoes.

**Q: Does the All-Marine Running Program have a Trial Camp?**

A: No, the All-Marine Running Program does not have an official Trial Camp.

**Q: Can a Marine participate in a Trial Camp if on leave?**

A: No, participation while in a leave status is prohibited.

**Q: Can a Marine participate while on Terminal Leave status?**

A: No, you have to be in an active status to participate.

**Q: Can a Marine take leave on the front or back of TAD?**

A: Marines must obtain Commander's approval for leave prior to creating DTS orders (except for emergency situations) and include leave details in DTS authorization.

**Q: What if my question is not answered here?**

A: You can send an email to: [AllMarineSports@usmc-mccs.org](mailto:AllMarineSports@usmc-mccs.org)

#### Athletes

**Q: What policy governs All-Marine Sports?**

**Q: Who is eligible for the All-Marine Sports Program?**

**Q: What sports are included in the All-Marine Sports Program?**

A: All sports listed on the [All-Marine Sports calendar](https://armedforcessports.defense.gov/Events-Calendar/) are currently offered.

**Q: My sport is not listed, can it be added?**

A: The inventory of sports is determined by Armed Forces Sports calendar, as established by the Armed Forces Sports Council, for each year.

# Intramural Sports

The Intramural Sports program offers a comprehensive range of team sports to promote a healthy lifestyle for Active Duty, family members and DoD civilians aboard the base of Quantico.

Intramural Sports provides a variety of athletic activities in which everyone can participate regardless of physical ability.

Units can compete for the Annual Commanders Cup Award.

**Athletics Eligibility**

The Marine Corps Base, Quantico Athletics program guarantees to provide a comprehensive range of individual and team sports for both men and women with an emphasis placed on mass participation. In addition, the program fulfills the leisure time needs of interested military personnel, their family members, and DoD civilians through recreational and competitive activities.

pages.text:
# Youth Sports

Youth Sports is a skill based program open to children ages 4-14.

## Youth Sports
Try outs are not required, as all skill levels are welcome to participate.

Semper Fit Youth Sports activities are open to all dependents of active duty, military reservists, retired military, and DOD employed civilians associated with MCAS Quantico, ages 4-14 unless specified otherwise. Registration dates are announced prior to each program or clinic and are subject to change. Fees, schedules, and age divisions are also subject to change.

The Youth Sports program offers seasonal baseball, basketball, flag football, cheerleading, and soccer. Summer Camps include baseball, flag football, cheer/hip hop, and basketball for ages 5-14. Registration periods are outlined below:

- **Baseball/Tee ball** Mid-February - Mid March
- **Summer Camps** Mid-May - Early August
- **Soccer** Late May - Early July
- **Flag Football** Early August - Mid-September
- **Basketball/Cheerleading** Early November - December

For practice and game cancellations or delays call the weather hotline.

**Pricing**
All sports seasons are $60, except for flag football which is $65.

**To become a youth sports coach the below is required:**

- Complete a Coaches Application and pass all background checks
- NAYS sports specific training (registered through youth sports office)
- Attend a mandatory child abuse course.
- Attend mandatory coaches orientation prior to the season

pages.text:
# Pools

MCCS offers a 50-meter pool, one- and three-meter diving boards, and a zero-entry wading pool with a slide and water feature. The facility also provides complete locker rooms with shower facilities. The MCCS pool is open only for Active Duty lap swim and military training from mid-May to last Friday in September.

**Refund, & Rain Check Policy** The pool will close in the event of thunder, lightning, or other inclement weather and will re-open 30 minutes after the last occurrence or at the discretion of the Pool Manager or designated staff member. All patrons must vacate the water and the pool deck during inclement weather. Patrons may wait in the locker rooms during the inclement weather but are prohibited from taking showers or using the sinks.

Pool Weather Hotline: [703.784.2973](tel:7037842973)

pages.text:
# Automotive Services

The Auto Skills Center provides assistance with repairs, maintenance, and instruction on automotive needs for Marines and their families.

## Tools and Facilities
- 6 Two post lifts for light duty cars /small SUVs /small trucks
- 2 Drive on oil change lifts (oil and lube only)
- Alignment Rack for alignments only, appointments only throughout the week no Saturdays
- 3 Heavy duty 12,000 lb lifts for full size trucks ½ ton to 1 ton
- 4 Flat stalls
- Quality tools
- Trained staff
- Engine room
- Storage space
- Tire machine and Balancer, staff performed service
- A/C Machine, staff performed service
- Various BG services coolant, brake, fuel, and trans services. Staff performed services
- Glass bead machine
- 2 Parts Washers

## For the safety of all patrons and staff, the following services are NOT permitted:
- Rust removal
- Rust proofing
- Rust neutralization
- Any body work (including sanding)
- Any service requiring respirators or masks

**FREE PRE-TRIP inspections for Active Duty and family members are performed only on dates and times specified on a first-come, first-served basis.**

- Inspections average 20-30 minutes, depending on make and model of vehicle.
- Patron must stay with vehicle.
- Copy of inspection results will be given to patron when inspection is completed
